articleTitle: Accurate Measurements of Energy, Efficiency and Power Quality in the Electric Railway System
abstract: This paper describes a new EU co-funded project on metrology for smart energy management is electric railway systems (MyRailS). The project involves 7 national metrology institutes, 3 universities and 6 railway companies. Research focusses on the following topics: i) new calibration facilities for energy meters on-board installed, ii) power quality monitoring systems, iii) accurate estimation of the saved energy by the installation of new reversible substations (RSS) and iv) by the adoption of eco-driving strategies.

articleTitle: Conducted EMI Causing Error Readings of Static Electricity Meters
abstract: Following initial studies showing that conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) can lead to large error readings of static electricity meters, VSL performed a thorough verification study confirming that wideband currents produced by non-linear, fast-switching loads indeed can lead to significant error readings of static meters. Key parameters of the EMI causing the errors are a short rise time and large peak height of the current step. When dimming linear or non-linear loads such as heaters and energy-saving lamps, the (lack of) internal filter in the dimmer has a large influence on these key parameters.

articleTitle: Evaluation of EMI Effects on Static Electricity Meters
abstract: Recent studies involving large errors in static electricity meters when exposed to step changes in the current waveform are reviewed. Triggered by these findings, a joint European research project has recently started to further evaluate these effects. A description is given of this pre-normative research programme which aims to provide evidence and techniques to resolve this unsatisfactory meter error situation. The need or otherwise for a regulatory and standardisation resnonse to these large meter errors is discussed.

articleTitle: Three Volt Pulse-Driven Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: We describe a new generation of Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizers that generate programmable ac waveforms with an rms amplitude of 3 V and, at 1 kHz, have a quantum locking range greater than 1 rnA. This system has two chips with a total of 204 960 Josephson junctions (JJs) co-located on a cryocooler. To test for systematic errors, we phase-shift by 180° the waveform generated by half the JJs (102 480 JJs) to produce an approximate null. The measured residual of 51 nV rms implies a relative agreement of 3 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> between the two halves of the system.

articleTitle: Estimation of Smart Meters Errors Using Meter Reading Data
abstract: This paper describes a method of online smart meter error calibration using meter reading data. An approach of data analysis using sum meter reading and branch meter reading in tree topology grid is studied. An algorithm based on the combination of K-means clustering and regularization theory is proposed to evaluate the smart meter error. The results of simulations based on real energy consumption data indicate the performance of the method.

articleTitle: Measurement of Absolute Phase Error of Digitizers
abstract: Some engineering applications, such as Phasor Measurement Unit and calibration of instrument transformers with digital output, require the knowledge of phase error of digitizers, to reach high phase measurement accuracy. This paper proposes a method for the measurement of digitizer absolute phase errors. The technique is based on the characterization of generator phase response and on the measurement of the time delay between the digitizer sampling clock and a phase reference signal. Taking into account the phase deviation introduced by generation system and the clock delay it is possible to accurately evaluate the digitizer absolute phase error.

articleTitle: Development of a WR-6 Waveguide Microcalorimeter for Thermoelectric Power Sensor
abstract: This paper reports recent development of a WR-6 (110 GHz - 170 GHz) rectangular waveguide microcalorimeter in China. This WR-6 microcalorimeter works as a national primary power measurement system, together with a newly designed and fabricated thermoelectric power sensor which is the transfer power standard. In this study, structure design of thermoelectric power sensor will be described, and preliminary measurement results for uncorrected effective efficiency of the power sensor using this WR-6 microcalorimeter will be reported.

articleTitle: Developing the Next Generation of NPL Kibble Balances
abstract: NPL is building a next generation Kibble balance to encourage more widespread primary realisations of the kilogram following the expected revision of the SI in 2019. The new balance does not require careful alignment of the coil and magnet and is aimed at a relative standard uncertainty of 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>. This paper describes progress on the development of the two technology demonstrator instruments which will guide the design of the next generation of Kibble balances at NPL.

articleTitle: Design and Modelling of a Shunt for Current Measurements at 10 a and up to 1 MHz: A Theoretical Approach
abstract: Electrical current shunts used as resistance standards in metrology laboratories are characterized by a broadband operating frequency bandwidth and are commonly calibrated up to 100 kHz. The use of a current shunt requires the preliminary knowledge of its magnitude deviation from DC and phase angle according to the frequency. The best magnitude performances published so far are limited to \pmb2 μΩ/Ω at 100 kHz. In this paper, we present an innovative shunt design for current measurements at 10 A up to 1 MHz. The relative deviation from DC is less than \pmb0.2 μΩ/Ω and \pmb20 μΩ/Ω in magnitude at 100 kHz and 1 MHz respectively.

articleTitle: Measurement of Supraharmonic Emissions (2 - 150 kHz) in Real Grid Scenarios
abstract: This paper describes the design of the measurement system for supraharmonic emissions in the frequency range 2 - 150 kHz in real grid scenarios and factors considered for design. It also portrays the validation of the measurement system on a smart grid platform and the design of experiments performed on this platform. Various network combinations and factors considered for real grid measurements are described in the paper.

articleTitle: Progress on PTB's Pulse-Driven Josephson Impedance Bridge Combined with an AC Quantum Hall Resistance
abstract: Pulse-driven Josephson arrays successfully demonstrated their high potential for impedance metrology in the last years. With their high spectral purity and fundamental accuracy, they are perfectly suited for impedance measurements over the whole complex plane. PTB's two-terminal impedance bridge is equipped with new electronics to extend the frequency range, to increase the signal amplitude and to simplify the setting of the phase angle. A 1:1 ratio measurement of 10 nF capacitance standards has been carried out between 246 Hz and 40 kHz at a signal amplitude of 75 mV (RMS). The value of a 10 nF capacitance standard is traced back to the ac quantum Hall resistor at PTB using 100 m V (RMS) signal amplitude.

articleTitle: A Novel Cognitive Neuromorphic Polarimetric Dynamic Vision System (pDVS) with Enhanced Discrimination and Temporal Contrast
abstract: In this preliminary study, a new cognitive vision architecture of a Polarimetric Dynamic Vision Sensor (pDVS), is presented. The system consists of a neuromorphic camera coupled to polarization filters; a spinning wheel, namely, a light modulating wheel, operating at different speeds, is placed in front a static object. The detector system performance against different modulating speeds, under unpolarized and polarized conditions, has been tested, data were acquired and then analyzed. The outcome of this study indicates that enhanced temporal contrast resolution can be achieved, while offering unique discrimination capabilities, depending upon the light polarization states.

Author Keywords: neuromorphic cognitive spike event-based Polarimetric Dynamic Vision Sensor (pDVS)

articleTitle: Towards a BIPM On-Site Comparison Program for AC Voltages Based on the Differential Sampling Technique
abstract: BIPM has conducted a few pilot studies to investigate the possibility of extending the protocol of the BIPM program of on-site DC Josephson Voltage Standard comparisons (BIPM.EM-KI0.b) to AC voltages. On-site indirect comparisons have been performed for AC low frequency sinewaves, at 1 V and 6.5 V rrns, using the new BIPM Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard and the differential sampling method. A relative agreement within a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> can typically be achieved using a commercial calibrator as a transfer standard. The noise of the phase locking process appears to be the limiting factor. We have been investigating other AC generators as possible candidates for an accurate transfer standard.

articleTitle: Comparison of Phase Angle Measurement Results by Means of Two Methods
abstract: The measurement results of the phase angle between two phase voltages are presented. The three-phase calibrator for metrological support of power quality analyzers was used as a source of voltages. These results are obtained by two methods: using a precision phase meter from the complement of State primary standard of phase angle unit and using a precision voltmeter. The type A uncertainty of measurement for both variants is evaluated, as well as the comparative analysis of measurement results is obtained.

articleTitle: The BIPM Kibble Balance for the Realization of the Redefined Kilogram
abstract: This paper reports the latest status of the Kibble balance experiment that the BIPM is developing for the realization of the upcoming redefined mass unit. The apparatus is now capable of working with a mass of 1 kg and fully operational in vacuum with a day-to-day repeatability at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> level. Studies are being conducted to evaluate various corrections such as those due to the coil-current effect and the self-attraction correction.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Precision Probe-Tilt Adjustment with the RF Signal Detection Technique
abstract: This study proposes a precision probe-tilt adjustment for an on-wafer measurement system. An original probe station with an electro-actuating goniometer stage was constructed to demonstrate the proposed technique. The tilt angle of a probe was shifted in the adjustment operation to acquire the S-parameter. The acquired S-parameter was analyzed to determine the angle of the goniometer stage, where the probe tip was aligned parallel to the substrate. The tilt angle was repeatedly estimated as ± 0.35 degree, which is over one degree in a conventional adjustment technique by direct observation with a microscope.

articleTitle: Trilateral Comparison of a Planar Thin-Film Thermal AC Voltage Standard in Frequency Range 1 MHz - 30 MHz
abstract: The paper presents results of a trilateral comparison of a travelling AC voltage standard, which was a fused-silica NIST planar multijunction thin-film thermal converter. The AC-DC voltage transfer difference of the standard was measured at 2 V and selected frequencies from 1 MHz to 30 MHz against primary thermal AC voltage standards at SUT, RISE and Trescal.

articleTitle: Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer as a Reference Standard for the Measurement of the Phase of Harmonics in Distorted Signals
abstract: We use the Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer to provide traceability for the phase of the harmonics, relative to its fundamental, of a distorted waveform. For distorted waveforms with rms values in the range from 0.154 V to 0.2 V and harmonic magnitudes from 5% to 40 % of the fundamental, our system can generate odd harmonics up to the 39<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> with phase uncertainties from 0.002° to 0.010<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>(k=2.0), depending on the harmonic number and harmonic magnitude.

articleTitle: Sampling AC Signals: Comparison of Fitting Algorithms and FFT
abstract: Fitting algorithms and FFT are commonly used to determine the RMS value and the phase of AC signals. This paper focusses on metrology applications and compares different algorithms with respect to their uncertainty contribution. The study covers pure sinewave signals, signals with noise and signals with cross-talk from a power line. The results are experimentally verified using an AC Josephson voltage source. The paper shows that the DC performance of the sampling system can be used for AC signals. The uncertainty contribution of the algorithms is negligible if the algorithm is chosen carefully.

articleTitle: Frequency Range Extension of the AC Quantum Voltmeter
abstract: A recently introduced coherent sub-sampling technique has been implemented to extend the frequency range of our AC quantum voltmeter up to 100 kHz. The measurement results are compared with differential sampling for frequencies up to 10 kHz. Above 3 kHz all preliminary results show a deviation from nominal values which increases quadratic with frequency. Possible error sources and corrections are discussed.

articleTitle: Shunt Module Development for Simple DC High-Current Measurements
abstract: To promote efficient use of direct current (DC) power, the authors have developed a shunt module for DC high current (SMHC), which enables simple measurement of DC high currents up to 1000 A. This paper explains the configuration and characteristics of our SMHC. We also report the results of basic tests performed on the parts that configure the prototype SMHC.

articleTitle: AC-DC Difference of a Thermal Transfer Standard Measured with a Pulse-Driven Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: An upgraded pulse-driven AC Josephson voltage standard system at the National Research Council Canada allows the generation of quantum-accurate root-mean-square voltages up to 1 V at frequencies down to 10 Hz. The system is used to determine the AC-DC difference of a commercial thermal transfer standard, and an uncertainty budget is presented. Such quantum voltage systems could replace aging multi-junction thermal converters.

articleTitle: The AC Quantum Voltmeter Used for AC Current Calibrations
abstract: In this work we present a method to use the AC quantum voltmeter setup for the measurement of ac currents up to 1 kHz frequencies. Besides the typical dc and ac voltage calibrations of programmable Josephson voltage standard arrays the area of application is extended. A commercial Fluke 5720A calibrator was investigated as current source in the frequency range from 10 Hz to a few kilohertz and it could be shown, that its stability and accuracy is much better than specified. The measured standard deviation in our setup varies from 0.5 μA/A to 5 μA/A.

articleTitle: Construction of New Shunts for a Wideband Sampling Wattmeter
abstract: This paper presents the status of the construction of current shunts from 20 mA to 100 A. They will be used as signal conditioners of a new standard for power measurements in the frequency range from 50 Hz to 100 kHz. The calibration in ratio is performed using ac-dc transfer difference while the phase calibration will be performed using a high-resolution, dual-channel digital sampling system.

articleTitle: Research on Output Characteristics of Magnetic Modulator Detection Winding
abstract: Mathematical model of magnetic modulator was established, characterized by the consistency with actual structure, which is two cores differential structure and excitation winding doubling as detection winding. Simulate and analyze the influence of excitation source (sine wave, triangle wave and square wave) and saturation depth of core on the output voltage of detection winding. The result shows that the output characteristic is optimal when employing square wave excitation source. Meanwhile, cores working in the over saturated state will lead to the oscillation of detection winding output waveform.

articleTitle: Application of Charge-Sensitive Preamplifier for the Calibration of Partial Discharge Calibrators Below 1 pC
abstract: Modern partial discharge calibrators often have their lowest range below 1 pC. However, traceable calibration services below 1 pC charges are not widely available, or their uncertainties are relatively high because of low signal levels. Application of charge-sensitive preamplifier for the calibration of partial discharge calibrators provides a promising solution. This new calibration method both improves signal level and integrates the partial discharge pulse. The characteristics of the preamplifier can be corrected using a software, but after that the partial discharge calibrator calibration results have good signal level and repeatability. Estimated uncertainty is below 2 % for 0.1 pC.

articleTitle: Development of WR-5 Waveguide Calorimeter for Millimeter Wave Power Standard
abstract: This paper reports a rectangular waveguide calorimeter for a WR-5 frequency band (140 GHz to 220 GHz). An SI traceable measurement of the absolute millimeter wave power with the calorimeter can be realized by DC substitution and correction with adiabatic efficiency, the DC substitution coefficient, transmission loss, scattering parameter, etc. As a result, we demonstrated that the developed calorimeter measured a millimeter wave power at a level of 0.5 mW, at a frequency range from 140 GHz to 220 GHz.

articleTitle: Interharmonic and Fundamental Phasor Estimator for Smart Grid Applications
abstract: With more and more renewable generations connnecting to power networks (such as wind power), the problem of subsynchronous oscillation (SSO) becomes increasingly prominent. The SSO are expressed as interharmonic components in currents/voltages, and may have a serious impact on power system stabilities. As a result, it is urgent to estimate interharmonic phasors for SSO monitoring. This paper introduces a novel method to estimate interharmonic and fundamental phasors with limited computational time and high accuracy.

articleTitle: WR-06 Power Standard Devices
abstract: A dc power substitution WR-06 calorimeter element was fabricated on a 500 um thick Si absorbing substrate. This element has now been used in NIM WR-06 power standard systems. The design uses integrated thermo resistive sensing and resistive power substitution elements deposited on the substrate The power absorbing layer, temperature sensor and heating resistor were integrated in the device.

articleTitle: Results of an International Comparison of Instrument Current Transformers up to 10 kA at 50 Hz Frequency
abstract: Traceability of the current ratio is crucial for the measurement of electrical energy in revenue metering. A comparison of the AC current ratio was therefore performed within EURAMET in the time period 2012 - 2016, using a precision CT as the traveling device. The Czech Metrology Institute (CMI) as coordinator processed the measurement results of the 15 European participating laboratories. The comparison of the results for transformer ratios of (4, 5, 6, 8, 10) kA/5 A at 15 VA burden and (4 and 10) kA/5 A ratios at 5 VA burden indicates good agreement between the participating laboratories. The main differences are found for phase displacement, at least in part due to instability of the traveling standard.

articleTitle: Comparison of PNS and Thermal Converter AC Voltage Measurements Between BIPM and NMIA Using a Sampling Voltmeter
abstract: We present the results of an indirect comparison of low-frequency ac voltage measurements between a programmable Josephson voltage standard at BIPM, and thermal-converter-based ac-dc transfer standards at NMIA. The measurements were conducted at frequencies from 62.5 Hz to 625 Hz and voltages from 0.8 V to 7 V using two sampling digital voltmeters as transfer standards. The ac-dc difference of the transfer standards was chosen as a comparison quantity due to its independence of the long-term drift of the gain of the transfer standards. The results show that the relative agreement degrades linearly from 0.1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> to 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> as the frequency increases from 62.5 Hz to 625 Hz. The metrological suitability of a sampling DVM used as a transfer standard is discussed.

articleTitle: Accurate High Direct Current Measurements for Industry
abstract: Calibration of high dc current transformers, dc ammeters, and dc current range extenders can be carried out simply using a high quality dc current transformer, an uncalibrated high current source and a calibrated low current source. The method, called the Current Reference Step Method, utilizes a buildup technique that exploits the ability that a de current transformer possesses to accurately sum the currents through its window with excellent differential linearity. Uncertainties of several parts per million in the applied high current can be achieved.

articleTitle: Step-Up Calibration of Resistive Voltage Dividers Using Two Sampling Digital Multimeters up to 50 kHz
abstract: A set of resistive voltage dividers was designed to be used in a measuring system of electric power up to 100 kHz. The calibration of the dividers based on the step-up method and a comparison system based on two Keysight-3458 digital multimeters working up to 50 kHz are described. This activity is part of a joint project of the National Metrology Institutes of Uruguay, Brazil and Argentina.

articleTitle: Calibration of an Inductive Voltage Divider Using Pulse-Driven Josephson Arrays
abstract: We present a method for the voltage ratio calibration of inductive voltage dividers using quantum accurate pulse-driven Josephson standards. The inductive voltage divider calibration is carried out at 497 Hz with RMS amplitudes of 40 mV and 100 mV and is compared with conventional bootstrapping calibrations performed at 1 V. In these preliminary measurements, the new calibration method reached similar in-phase uncertainties as the bootstrapping method, despite the large difference in input voltages.

articleTitle: A New Measurement Method for Supraharmonics in 2–150 kHz
abstract: The 32 equal-width segments supraharmonics measurement method, recommended in the newly revised standard IEC 61000-4-30, has some disadvantages, such as the large frequency resolution, and the large effect of spectral leakage. To overcome this, a new measurement method for supraharmonics in 2-150 kHz based on compressive sensing is proposed. Simulation results and measured data analysis indicate that the proposed approach can overcome DFT algorithm's limitation, and the frequency resolution can be improved by an order-of-magnitude without extending the signal's observation time. The amplitude of supraharmonics can also be calculated accurately.

articleTitle: Radio-Frequency Waveform Synthesis with the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: We have measured the output power versus synthesis frequency (transfer function), up to 100 MHz, of a modified Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer. A 50 Ω resistor was integrated within the Josephson junction array circuit to match the nominally zero array impedance to a 50 Ω transmission line and load. The resistor significantly reduces ripple in the transfer function due to reflections from impedance mismatches, but it reduces the output voltage by a factor of two. The measured power is constant within 0.01 dB up to 10 MHz, above which it deviates by no more than 0.15 dB.

articleTitle: The Project “Metrology for Inductive Charging of Electric Vehicles”
abstract: The European metrology programme for innovation and research (EMPIR) is the current main programme for European research on metrology. In 2016, within the EMPIR call, the project “Metrology for inductive charging of electric vehicles” (MICEV) was approved and it started in September 2017. Inductive charging is a wireless charging technology that will be widely used with electric vehicles (EVs) in the near future, offering many advantages over traditionally fuelled and current EVs. The project aims to advance inductive power transfer (IPT) for EV charging by developing metrology techniques for measuring power transfer efficiency and reliable demonstration of compliance with existing safety standards for human exposure. The main research topics are: measurement of the power transmitted on-board, transmission efficiency, requirements for measurements in the dynamic charging, assessment of magnetic field exposure.

articleTitle: A Sampling-Based Ratio Bridge for Calibrating Voltage Transformers
abstract: This paper describes the setup of a sampling-based ratio bridge for calibrating voltage transformers. The advantage of this ratio method is that voltage transformers with different transformer ratios can be easily compared. Initial measurements of the components of the bridge indicate low systematic errors, negligible voltage dependency and low phase errors around 50 / 60 Hz. This indicates an attainable uncertainty of below 2 ppm for the ratio error and \pmb0.5 μ rad for the phase displacement of voltage transformers.

articleTitle: AC Voltage Measurements up to 120 V with a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer and an Inductive Voltage Divider
abstract: We use a precision inductive voltage divider and a lock-in amplifier to extend the voltage range of a Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer with a maximum voltage of 250 mV rms to provide accurate voltage measurements up to 120 V. Experimental results show that the output of the JAWS can be extended to high voltages with uncertainties of a few microvolts per volt or less, depending on the voltage amplitude and frequency.

articleTitle: Trilateral South American Project: A Reference System for Measuring Electric Power Up to 100 kHz - Progress Report
abstract: Three countries in South America are jointly developing a reference system for measuring electric power up to 100 kHz. The objective is the construction of three similar measuring systems, one for each institute. The measuring system and the current status of the development of its modules are described here. This project will contribute to provide calibration services in measuring ranges still not covered by the three institutes both in ac-dc transfer and in electric power.

articleTitle: Time Latency of DC Input Path for 3458A Sampling Multimeter
abstract: The Keysight 3458A is a common digitizer because of the great accuracy and small integration time. The bandwidth of its DC input path varies depending on the magnification of input amplifier of different ranges, which causes time latency of input signal. A method to measure the latency based on aperture time is introduced. When the aperture approximately equals to the period of the signal under test, extremum of sampling value reflects signal's initial phase. Experiments at 1V and 10V ranges with input signals of 25kHz and 50kHz were carried out and the time latency were measured. Then the bandwidth were calculated which were the same of about 120kHz for these two ranges.

articleTitle: D-Band Waveguide Microcalorimeter for Millimeter-Wave Power Standard
abstract: This paper introduces a D-band waveguide microcalorimeter for the millimeter-wave power standard in Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science. The brief design scheme of the microcalorimeter is presented. Some considerations for the implementation of major parts are presented.

articleTitle: Helium-Based Refractometry for Pressure Measurements in the Range 1–100 kPa
abstract: This paper describes an alternative of pressure measurements based on a helium absolute refractometer at 532 nm. The Fabry-Perot cavity has been characterized from relevant parameters and the resolution in pressure of this new optical pressure sensor is lower than 0.2 Pa.

articleTitle: VNIIM 10 V Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: A 10 V programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) was developed at VNIIM on the basis of a Supracon 10 V chip. The current margins for the first Josephson step are close to 1 mA. This programmable system was directly compared with a conventional dc Josephson voltage standard (JVS) based on 10 V PTB chip in the range from 1 mV to 10 V.

articleTitle: A Table-Top Graphene Quantized Hall Standard
abstract: We report the performance of a quantum standard based on epitaxial graphene maintained in a 5 T table-top cryocooler system. The v=2 resistance plateau, with a value of R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K-90</sub>/2, is used to scale to 1 kΩ using a binary cryogenic current comparator (BCCC) bridge. The preliminary uncertainties achieved with the BCCC are like those obtained in state-of-the-art measurements using GaAs-based devices. This quantum standard requires no liquid He and can operate continuously, allowing year-round accessibility to traceable resistance measurements.

articleTitle: Precision Buffer with Low Input Capacitance
abstract: This paper describes precision voltage follower (buffer) circuit designed for precision measurement purposes. Presented buffer was designed for use at frequencies up to 1 MHz and voltage amplitude up to 1.5 V. Buffer has input capacitance below 1 pF. Output impedance at 100 kHz is below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11 \ \text{m}\Omega$</tex>. Amplitude and phase transfer error is below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \ \mu\text{V}/\text{V}$</tex> and 2 μrad at 100 kHz. Error of the transfer at 1 MHz depends on the used output cable and load. The error was less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \ \mu \text{V}/\text{V}$</tex> with the 20cm cable.

articleTitle: Establishment of an Instrument Transformer Calibration System at SASO NMCC
abstract: A calibration system for instrument transformers, based on the comparison method, has been established at SASO NMCC. Ratio error and phase displacement measurements are performed by using the calibration system up to 4000 A for current transformers and up to 36 kV for voltage transformers at 60 Hz. Calibration uncertainties for both current and voltage transformers are well below the industrial and metrological needs in the country. Bilateral comparisons between SASO NMCC and TÜBİTAK UME have been performed in order to evaluate the performance of the calibration system.

articleTitle: Timestamping Type 3458A Multimeter Samples
abstract: Often, AC signals are sampled using type 3458A digital multimeters in DC mode with an external trigger signal. Different algorithms can be used to determine RMS value and phase of the signal of interest. Especially when the phase information is required, knowledge about the timing is essential. This can be achieved modifying the clock source of the multimeter, forcing the multimeter to operate on an external clock and removing the synchronisation jitter of the trigger input TRIG IN. Another option is to use the EXT OUT signal generated by the multimeter for timestamping. This paper compares both methods.

articleTitle: Characterizing OMNI-Directional Antenna by Complex Normalized Effective Height Based on Broadband Calculable Antennas
abstract: The complex normalized effective height (CNEH) is used to characterize omni-directional antennas based on a novel method. There is no phase information for the traditional parameters such as effective length and antenna gain. In contrast CNEH is a “versatile'” parameter for many applications. A pair of super broadband precise calculable dipole antennas (CDAs) and calculable biconical antennas are used to experimentally verify this. The difference of CNEH between measurements and simulations is less than 0.37 dB and 4 degree from 10 MHz to 1.5GHz. Better results can be achieved with more dipoles.

articleTitle: An Active Low-Voltage Capacitor for Capacitive HV Dividers
abstract: This paper describes the setup of an active low-voltage capacitor designed to realize capacitive voltage dividers by means of compressed-gas, high-voltage capacitors for rated primary voltages between 5 kV and 800 kV/√3. In the future, this divider, which has a negligible voltage dependency and low phase errors around 50/60 Hz, will be used to realize a fundamental step-up calibration method for the standard voltage transformers at PTB. Initial measurements indicate an attainable uncertainty of below 2 ppm for the ratio error (short-term) and 1 μrad for the phase displacement of the capacitive divider.

articleTitle: Calibration of AC Voltage for a High Speed Sampling ADC Board Using Thermal Voltage Converters
abstract: This paper describes a calibration technique for a commercial Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) board using Thermal Voltage Converters (TVCs) up to 1 MHz with various sampling rates. The DC voltage was calibrated first. Then, AC-DC transfer difference of the ADC board was measured by comparing it with a standard TVC. The AC voltage error was calculated by using both calibration results. The estimated expanded uncertainty of the AC voltage error for 0.5 Vrms was less than 70 μV in 1-V range of the ADC for all sampling rates.

articleTitle: Measurement of Leakage Current to Ground in Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards
abstract: The voltage error associated with the leakage current of programmable Josephson voltage standards (PJVS) is one of the largest contributions to the uncertainty in direct comparison of voltage standards. Due to the parallel biasing scheme of the PJVS and the resulting multiple leakage paths, the quantities “leakage resistance” and “leakage current” are not necessarily equivalent. A method to measure and model the leakage current to ground for a given PJVS output voltage is presented. By upgrading simple components of the NIST system, the leakage current to ground can be reduced from 250 pA to 50 pAat 10 V.

articleTitle: A Broadband Two-Channel Sigma-Delta Digitizer for Power Measurement - Design Concepts
abstract: This paper describes a broadband two-channel digitizer based on a high-resolution, Sigma-Delta analogue-to-digital converter with an input voltage range of ±1 V, to measure electric power from DC to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent Verification of the Quantum Accuracy of a Quantum Voltage Noise Source
abstract: This paper describes the characterization of a quantum voltage noise source (QVNS) based on pulse-driven Josephson-arrays for frequencies up to 200 kHz. The QVNS synthesizes a voltage noise reference which is used to calibrate the electronics of a Johnson noise thermometer (JNT). To realize an “electronic Kelvin” with measurement uncertainty at μK/K -level, we investigated the frequency-dependent voltage difference between two pulse-driven Josephson Arrays, each one producing a 10 mV RMS sinusoidal voltage.

articleTitle: Determination of AC-DC Transfer Difference of SUT Calculable Thermal Voltage Converters in 1 MHz - 30 MHz Frequency Range
abstract: The paper presents results of determination of the AC-DC voltage transfer differences in 1 MHz - 30 MHz frequency range of the two reference thermal voltage converters developed at Silesian University of Technology (SUT). Two experimental methods confirmed high accuracy of results obtained from the mathematical model.

articleTitle: Field Testing of ROCOF Algorithms in Multiple Locations on Bornholm Island
abstract: The importance of rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) measurements in electrical power grids is discussed along with its measurement challenges. A measurement campaign in a renewable-rich grid to compare ROCOF measurement algorithms with a variety of configurations at multiple locations is presented. An example of a captured ROCOF event is given.

articleTitle: Measurement Uncertainty Analysis for On-Wafer TRL Calibration Using Precision RF Probing Technique
abstract: The paper demonstrates measurement uncertainty analysis in on-wafer measurement with detail discussion of probe tilt and stage rotation. Since ours measurement system can realize repeatable determination of probe position in X-, Y-, and Z-axes, influences of probe tilt and stage rotation can be evaluated with the system avoiding influences regard to variations in probe coordinates. Uncertainty-analysis algorithm was constructed for the analysis of each uncertainty contributor in case of conventional manual probing and precision probing technique. Consequently, measurement uncertainty with the precision probing technique was a half of conventional manual probing technique.

articleTitle: SI Traceable Small Mass Measurement Using the Voltage Balance Apparatus at NMIJ
abstract: For establishing a new calibration method for small mass and force based on a new definition of the kilogram, the SI traceable measurement method which uses the electrostatic force balance was developed. Small mass was measured by comparing the gravity force acting on the small object and the electrostatic force which can be calibrated by using the electrical standards. New technical approaches such as monolithic flexure hinge for balance mechanism and double equal capacitor system for electrical control were applied. Weighing of a 2 mg stainless steel weight was performed. In the measurement, there was deviation from the nominal value of the weight, which was caused by the thermal drift and surface charge. Details on the measurement apparatus and the experiment results are presented.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Propagation and Evaluation of Nano-Scale Stray Field in Quantitative Magnetic Force Microscopy Measurements
abstract: It is essential for a traceable magnetic field calibration to understand how data processing methods impact the final result. Here, we report a quantitative nano-scale magnetic stray field characterization method, which is based on phase images measured by magnetic force microscopy, combined with a magnetic tip calibration procedure and Wiener deconvolution in Fourier domain. We discuss components and propagation of uncertainties in the tip calibration procedure and in the stray field calculation. An evaluation procedure is proposed and the measurement uncertainty of the stray field for a test sample SmCo5 is evaluated.

articleTitle: Rabi Resonance Measurements Based on CS Vapor Cell for Microwave Magnetic Field Detection in Free Space
abstract: In this paper we characterized the lineshapes of Rabi resonances for microwave (MW) magnetic field with cesium vapor cell in free space. The relation between resonance lineshapes and phase modulation frequency under different experimental parameters are investigated. Based on the obtained lineshapes, the evaluation of Rabi frequency has been done in free space. Optimal laser intensity and cell temperature are obtained in our experiment, preliminary analysis of the experimental results is reported.

articleTitle: A Method for Measurement of Step Voltage Rise Time of Partial Discharge Calibrators
abstract: The measurement methods of the step voltage risetime of Partial Discharge calibrators are discussed. A method using a capacitor is recommended in the latest edition of IEC standard(IEC 60270-2015). However, the influences by the capacitance of cables and the capacitive component of the input impedance of the oscilloscope should not be neglected in the former method, especially for the measurement of the low-quantity discharge. A method for the measurement of the rise time of the step voltage by connecting a resistor to PD calibrators is presented. This method is more suitable for the measurement of charge transfers less than hundreds of picocoulombs.

articleTitle: The MSL Kibble Balance Weighing Mode
abstract: MSL is developing a Kibble balance for realizing the kilogram after it is redefined in terms of the Planck constant. The MSL Kibble balance has the potential to achieve an accuracy (standard uncertainty) of about 2 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. It is based on twin pressure balances to simplify the alignment of the coil and magnetic field axes with each other, and with local gravity. The pressure balances also act as a force comparator in the weighing mode. This approach contrasts with other Kibble balances which use a beam balance or wheel for the force comparator.

articleTitle: Design of a Distributed UHF Sensor Array System for PD Detection and Location in Substation
abstract: This paper describes a distributed system for partial discharge (PD) detection and location in substation. The proposed system is composed of several UHF antennas located dispersedly and form an array. These antennas are connected to the central control room by optical fiber using radio over fiber technique to decrease the propagation attenuation of the PD signal. the scatter layout increases the coverage of PD signal sensing and the time difference of arrived partial discharge signals propagating to the antennas, so that the location accuracy of the PD source can be improved. The desired result is obtained by experiment in substation.

articleTitle: Realisation of Absolute Phase and Ac Resistance of Current Shunts by Ratio Measurements
abstract: This article presents a method for realising absolute phase and ac resistance for current shunts using only impedance ratio measurements. The method is based on three geometrically identical current shunts with different resistances, but with the same inductance, capacitance and ac resistance (change of resistance at ac compared to dc), We demonstrate how the inductance, capacitance and ac resistance can be calculated from the complex impedance ratio measurements, thereby realising absolute current shunt impedance. This method simplifies the procedure of current shunt calibration, since the same impedance ratio setup which is used to compare a shunt to a reference shunt, is used to realise the impedance of the starting reference shunt.

articleTitle: A Voltage Calibration Chain for Meters Used in Measurements of EV Inductive Power Charging
abstract: The inductive charging of electric vehicles requires specific measurement and calibration systems. In fact, the measurement of power on board involves DC signals, which are superimposed to a significant AC ripple up to or over 150 kHz, depending on the type of charging system. A calibration method that makes use of a phantom power, based on two independent but synchronized circuits, is considered, simulating the charging voltage and current. This paper describes in detail a solution in the realization of the voltage calibration chain, based on the use of a DC voltage calibrator, an injector and a voltage divider.

articleTitle: Determination of Voltage Dependence in High-Voltage Standard Capacitors
abstract: The voltage coefficient of pressured gas capacitors is a relevant parameter in high-voltage calibrations. These capacitors, used as standards, are calibrated at low voltages, so that it is necessary to know their variation when they are used at high voltages. Although several methods have been proposed to determine that coefficient, their implementations are very difficult. In this paper, a simplified method is proposed, that does not need of any special equipment, so that it is easy to achieve for most high-voltage laboratories.

articleTitle: Temperature Chamber with Precise Temperature Stability
abstract: This paper describes a system to maintain stable air temperature in a temperature chamber. The aim of the system is to stabilize temperature of resistance standards during measurements. Particular attention was paid to provide precise air temperature stabilization. The construction of temperature chamber and the results of long-term tests are also presented.

articleTitle: Modeling the Nonlinear Amplifier with the Pulse-Driven AC Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: Behavior models of electronic components are critical in many metrological and measurement areas. This paper uses a two-tone signal synthesized by the pulse-driven ac Josephson voltage standard to achieve the input/output behavior of a nonlinear amplifier. Three Volterra series models including the memory polynomial model, general memory polynomial model, and dynamic deviation reduction model are analyzed and compared in detail. The result demonstrates the high performance of the achieved mathematical models.

articleTitle: 10 MΩ Quantum Hall Array Device
abstract: We have developed 10 kΩ and 1 MΩ quantum Hall array devices so far on GaAs/AlGaAs substrates. To realize higher quantized resistance, we designed \pmb10 MΩ array device. The 10 MΩ quantum Hall array device consists of simply serially connected 775 Hall bars, and its nominal value is 10 MΩ×(1+246.27 μΩ/Ω). The channel width is 35 μm, and the expected collapse current is over 20 μA for each Hall bar. The Hall bars are connected with triple-connection technique to avoid the influence of contact resistance and wiring resistance on the quantized resistance value.

articleTitle: Phase Error Calibration of Current Shunts at Power Frequencies Using AC-Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: We have established a measurement method to calibrate phase error of current shunts with currents from 10 mA to 80 A at power frequencies using differential sampling technique based on an AC-programmable Josephson voltage standard (AC-PJVS). Evaluation results show that the expanded uncertainty of the phase error of current shunts calibrated by AC-PJVS is \pmb0.80×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> degree or 14 \pmbμrad \pmb(k=2) at 50 Hz and 62.5 Hz. For current shunts used in measurement of power standards, the uncertainty is sufficient. These researches are very helpful in establishing the self-traceability of our power standards at the Center for Measurement Standards (CMS) in Taiwan.

articleTitle: Effect of Input Bandwidth of a Sampler on Differential Sampling Based on a Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: We have investigated the response characteristics of two different samplers, Keysight 3458A and NI 5922 implemented in setup for differential sampling based on a programmable Josephson voltage standard, to input signals in a frequency range below 1 kHz. The RMS amplitudes measured with the samplers coincides within a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> at frequencies below 100 Hz. However, the difference between the RMS values increases with the frequency, mainly due to the dramatic change of the value obtained with the Keysight 3458A. The difference reaches up to 25 μV/V at 1 kHz. The feature is inferred to originate from the difference in the input bandwidths for the two samplers.

articleTitle: Parameterization Models for Traceable Characterization of Planar CPW SOL Calibration Standards
abstract: Methods for traceable characterization and uncertainty evaluation of planar 1-port CPW short-open-Ioad (SOL) devices are developed. The agreement of modelling and verification measurement results greatly supports the application of the proposed parameterization models and used FEM-based EM modelling of CPW structures for traceable characterization of planar CPW-based SOL devices in the frequency range between a few kHz up to 50 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling Wideband Cage-Type Current Shunts
abstract: A survey was made of several cage-type current shunts commercially available and/or developed by National Metrology Institutes. One design was selected from those as prospectively having a large bandwidth. A lumped equivalent circuit model for current shunts assembled according to this design is summarized here. The ac-dc difference and phase displacement of shunts with nominal currents from 0.5 A to 20 A are computed using standard two-port network theory.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Uncertainty of Self-Calibrating VNA Procedures
abstract: Some important vector network analyzer (VNA) calibration procedures, such as thru-reflect-line (TRL), are not amenable to uncertainty analysis by conventional methods, because the calibration equations do not refer to the standards used. Nevertheless, by relating small changes in standard S-parameter values to corresponding changes in VNA response, sensitivity coefficients for the error coefficients obtained by calibration can be evaluated indirectly. The approach is easily implemented with uncertain-number software.

articleTitle: High Voltage Capacitance Bilateral Intercomparison Between INTI and UTE
abstract: A bilateral intercomparison between National Metrology Institutes of Argentina (INTI) and Uruguay (UTE) was done on high voltage capacitance. The traveling standard was a 400 kV, 50 pF, SF6 gas capacitor. Several influence factors on the measurement uncertainty are analyzed.

articleTitle: Uncertainty of the Ohm Using Cryogenic and Non-Cryogenic Bridges
abstract: We describe recent scaling measurements to decade resistance levels based on both cryogenic and non-cryogenic current comparator bridges. National measurement institutes and the International Bureau of Weights and Measures derive traceability for the SI ohm using the quantum Hall effect, with the primary comparisons made at the resistance value R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k-90</sub>/2 = 12906.4035 Ω. Cryogenic current comparator scaling methods are preferred since large resistance ratios of 100 or more are achieved with unsurpassed uncertainty. The quantized Hall resistance standard based on graphene allow less complex and more cost-effective room-temperature resistance bridges to provide SI traceability.

articleTitle: On the Development of an AC-Quantum Voltmeter
abstract: This paper presents an AC-Quantum voltmeter based on a 1 V programmable Josephson array, a purpose-built sigma-delta digitizer, a clock generator and a custom AC bias source. The highlights of this system are briefly described and supported by preliminary measurements.

articleTitle: Precision Characterisation of Current Transformers and Shunts in the Audio Frequency Range
abstract: This paper presents a technique to compare two current transformers, or a current transformer and ac current shunts, with an uncertainty better than 1 uA/A and 1 urad at audio frequencies. Examples of such a comparison at frequencies from 10Hz to 10kHz are given. Due to its low uncertainty, the described technique made it possible to accurately measure critical parameters such as common-mode dependence of a current transformer and impedance variation of current shunts with ac current applied.

articleTitle: Broadband Permittivity Measurements Using a Frequency-Variable Balanced-Type Circular-Disk Resonator
abstract: We have experimentally verified that the balanced-type circular-disk (BCD) resonator method can provide permittivity measurements at almost arbitrary frequency points by changing the size of the circular disk that constitutes the resonator. Resonant frequencies of the BCD resonator can be changed by replacing the expendable parts instead of including a movable part in the resonator. We clarified that a highly stable and rather simple permittivity measurements at a desired frequency point can be realized with the BCD resonator by demonstrating the consistency of measured permittivities of a low-loss material obtained with five circular disks with different radii.

articleTitle: A Programmable Bias Source for the PJVS in the BIPM Kibble Balance
abstract: This paper describes a bias source that has been developed to configure the Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard used in the BIPM Kibble Balance. It has thirteen channels based on thirteen current sources with floating output. The operation of the bias source has been verified with PJVS system, exhibiting accuracy on the reference voltage at the \pmb10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> level.

articleTitle: Study on the Frequency Bandwidth Limits for Deconvolution of the Step Response
abstract: A non-ideal step response of the digitizer may introduce significant errors in the impulse voltage measurement. Deconvolution is a good method to correct the step response. However, it is sensitive to noise. We studied on the influence of the frequency bandwidth limit on the deconvolution processing, with the results reported in this paper. This correction method was applied to the step responses recorded with three different commercial digitizers, and the error introduced by the corrected step responses were all reduced to less than 0.1%, which would be negligible in the impulse measurement.

articleTitle: Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards Comparisons at 10 V-DC, 1 V and 7 V RMS, 50 Hz Between BIPM and CENAM
abstract: Within a program of BIPM pilot studies, the new Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) of the BIPM and that of CENAM were compared directly at 10 V DC. In AC, the PJVSs were compared indirectly at 1 V and 7 V rms, 50 Hz, using a commercial calibrator as a transfer standard. A relative agreement of few tens of pV/V could be achieved in DC and a relative agreement of few tenths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pmb{\mu} \mathbf{V}/\mathbf{V}$</tex> could be reached in AC. The main uncertainty source in AC is the measurements dispersion coming from the phase noise of the calibrator output.

articleTitle: Measure of the Absolute Phase Angle of a Power Frequency Sinewave with Respect to UTC
abstract: This paper presents a method to measure the absolute phase angle of a power frequency sinewave with respect to the passage of the UTC second. The need for such a technic arises during the calibration or adjustment of PMUs or SAMUs. The accuracy of these instruments depends on their ability to measure the absolute phase. The principle of the method is based on a phase comparison between a sine wave and the fundamental component of a square wave of identical frequency. The absolute phase angle of the square wave is first established against the PPS signal of an atomic clock.

articleTitle: Error Analysis of an AC Voltage Differential Sampling System
abstract: This paper analyzes error sources of a differential sampling system. We derive the error transfer function and prove that the effect of gain error on the accuracy of the reconstructed sine wave measurement is significantly reduced by a switching method. The relationship between the differential coefficient and the differential signal have been analyzed. It is concluded that if the RMS amplitude error of sine wave being less than 0.05 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{V}/\mathrm{V}$</tex>, the system gain error should be less than 46 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{V}/\mathrm{V}$</tex> when the number of steps is 40 or greater.

articleTitle: Keysight 3458A Frequency Response Model Identification
abstract: This paper describes a measurement and a model parameter identification of Keysight 3458A frequency response in sampling mode. When modeling the frequency response with aperture time sinc roll-off, single pole low pass filter and linear input capacitance dissipation factor roll-off, a better than 20 μV/V linearity and ac voltage accuracy can be achieved in the audio frequency band on 1 V range.

articleTitle: Null Technique for Precision RF Phase Shift Measurements
abstract: A dual channel IF substitution null system is developed for precision phase shift measurements and standards in frequency ranges of 1 MHz to 1 GHz. A particular programmable IF phase shifter equipped with a calibrated phase monitor is used as a phase reference standard. High sensitivity nature of the null technique provides accurate measurements to the DUT even with large attenuation. Measurement resolutions of 0.002 deg., 0.006 deg., and 0.023 deg. were obtained for DUT with attenuation of 20 dB, 40 dB, and 60 dB, respectively, at 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Comparison of Sampling Voltage Measurements of Multi-Tone Signals
abstract: This paper describes results of a comparison of voltage amplitude measurements of complex waveform signals. A stable arbitrary waveform generator was used as a transfer standard and sent between four institutes in a round loop. Participants used different digitizers, different sampling configurations and algorithms to measure the signal voltage and to calculate the amplitudes of harmonic components.

articleTitle: Comparison of two Reference Setups for Calibration of Power Transformer Loss Measurement Systems
abstract: A comparison has been performed of the VSL and PTB reference setups for the calibration of industrial power transformer loss measurement systems (TLMS). Both setups are developed within the “ELPOW” European joint research project, with the aim to calibrate industrial TLMS as a complete system, rather than just via its individual components, with an overall uncertainty of better than \pmb50 μ W/VA, for voltages up to 100 kV, currents up to 2 kA, and power factors down to zero. The initial comparison results show excellent agreement of the PTB and VSL reference setups, with typical differences less than \pmb15 μ W/VA, well within the uncertainty of the setups.

articleTitle: Optical Frequency Stabilization at the 10−16 Fractional Level Utilizing Ramsey-Borde Atom Interferometry
abstract: We demonstrate laser frequency stabilization at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> fractional frequency level in one second through spectroscopy on a 650 °C calcium atomic beam. The calcium beam is interrogated with a cavity stabilized 657 nm laser arranged in a Ramsey-Borde configuration. A second laser at 431 nm reads off the final atomic state populations while allowing for high signal-to-noise. Limitations of this method are being explored and, and, based on current noise analysis, there is potential to achieve fractional frequency stabilities in the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-17</sup> range or below.

articleTitle: Mechanical Improvements and Investigations on the LNE new Thompson-Lampard Calculable Capacitor
abstract: To improve the traceability of the unit of capacitance in the SI with a relative standard uncertainty of about one part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>, a new Thompson-Lampard calculable capacitor is currently developed at LNE. This paper presents the progress on the alignment of the electrodes and the positioning of the movable guard in the cavity.

articleTitle: Inter-Laboratory Nanoamp Current Comparison with Sub-Part-Per-Million Uncertainty
abstract: An ultrastable low-noise current amplifier (ULCA) has been transferred between two laboratories, NPL and PTB, four times, with three of the transfers yielding a relative change in the trans-resistance gain of less than 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>. This is a new benchmark for inter-laboratory transfer of small current.

articleTitle: Calibration of Electrometers with Sub-PPM Accuracy
abstract: We performed calibrations of different commercial picoammeters using the `Ultrastable Low-noise Current Amplifier' (ULCA) operated in current source mode as calibrator in the current range between 1 fA and 1 μA. The results allow the comprehensive characterization of the devices under test regarding noise, settling and burden voltage behavior as well as stability of the gain factor, and confirm the superior performance of the ULCA for use as small current calibrator standard.

articleTitle: Power Measurement at Wireless Transmission of Electricity in the Frequency Range from 0.01 to 10 MHz
abstract: Searching for design optimization of a wireless power transmission system based on open loop resonance circuits. Main parameters measuring, conclusions on design variants, using of transfer power broadband wattmeter with own consumption error correction for losses minimization.

articleTitle: Characterization of High-Temperature Superconducting Tapes
abstract: The article presents a measurement system for determination of relation between critical current and magnitude and angle of external magnetic field of high-temperature superconductors (HTS). The obtained characteristics can be used as an input data to numerical calculations or simulations of HTS tapes and cables.

articleTitle: 1 V AC-DC Difference of a Thermal Transfer Standard Measured with a Pulsed Josephson Standard Unloaded by a Transconductance Amplifier
abstract: A transconductance amplifier (TCA) with a negative admittance has been used in parallel with a commercial thermal transfer standard (TTS) to unload the voltage source, a pulse-driven AC Josephson Voltage Standard (also known as Josepson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer or JAWS). AC-DC difference measurements at 1 V and at frequencies from 10Hz to 10kHz show excellent agreement with the values obtained by a conventional method. Expanded uncertainties between \pmb0.28 μ V/V and \pmb0.39 μ V/V\pmb(k=2), depending on the frequency, have been achieved.

articleTitle: Performance of Reference Partial Discharge Measurement System
abstract: Electrical insulation problems emerge while decreasing energy losses by the use of high voltage. Several tests are carried out in the laboratory to determine the electrical insulation problems such as partial discharge (PD) test. Due to the requirement of high accuracy of PD test, the reference measurement systems with low uncertainty are needed. Standard PD measurement system consists of two parts, PD detector, and calibrator. The most important role of the precise PD measurements belongs to the calibrator. This paper presents here the performance of reference measuring system developed in TÜBİTAK UME for the calibration of PD calibrators.

articleTitle: Current Divider Based Impedance Comparator
abstract: The paper describes an ac impedance measurement comparator system which uses a current divider (or splitter). The divider makes use of a current comparator whose windings are connected in a way such as to allow the splitting of a single current signal in two components with very accurate ratio to be attained. Each current component flows through impedances to be compared. Preliminary investigations indicate that such an arrangement is able to provide very accurate impedance measurements with errors of parts in \pmb10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> or even smaller. Resolutions of parts in \pmb10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> were also experimentally achieved. Since the system uses a single ac current source, inherent current instabilities of the source cause negligible effects on differential voltage measurements, what alleviates requirements on the ac source. Digital sampling can easily be implemented with the system for speeded-up and automated impedance comparisons.

articleTitle: The Coil-Current Effect in the Joule Balance with Bifilar Coil and Compensation Coils Applied
abstract: Bifilar coil can be used in the Kibble/joule balance to improve the equivalence of magnetic factor Bl in the two measurement phases. In the joule balance, compensation coils are applied to reduce the effect of external field. When the bifilar coil and compensation coils are used together in the joule balance, the coil current effect is analyzed in this paper. It is found that the magnetic factor change in the velocity phase is about 2.3 times as the value obtained in the weighing phase.

articleTitle: Shielding Performance Evaluation of BIPM-Type Kibble Balance Magnet
abstract: How the background magnetic flux (far field) affects the magnetic field in a BIPM-type Kibble balance magnet is investigated. The field coupling paths along both the vertical and the horizontal directions are discussed based on finite element analysis. It is found that the vertical background coupling can contribute to the mean value of the radial field in the air gap while the horizontal background flux can only produce a weak torque in the weighing phase. The discussion helps to understand potential systematic errors in different realizations of Kibble balance measurements, especially for a magnet-moving balance.

articleTitle: Experience with Current Transformer Calibration System Based on Rogowski Coil
abstract: This paper discusses experience with current transformer calibration system based on the Rogowski coil. Rogowski coil has no ferromagnetic material in the core and thus the coil cannot be saturated. This means that the coil has inherently excellent linearity. It can be calibrated with low current using a current shunt. The system was taken into use in 2003. Stability of the system is demonstrated, and experience with using the coil is summarized. Proven overall uncertainty in routine calibration work is 0.0025 % for ratio error and 50 μrad for phase displacement up to 8 kA.

articleTitle: Methods for Electrical Cooling and Thermometry of a Suspended Silicon Chip
abstract: We suspend a heavily doped conducting silicon chip by tunnel junctions and aluminum leads, which permits the measurement and control of electrical and phonon heat fluxes. Experiments and analysis on heat conduction and electrical cooling utilize techniques developed for electron pumps and primary thermometry, and the techniques developed for the cooler may also be useful for the development quantum phase slip based devices.

articleTitle: Calibration of Current Shunt Standards in the Megahertz Region
abstract: Beyond 1 A (from 2 A to 100 A typically) standard current shunts are currently calibrated in magnitude up to 100 kHz and in phase angle up to 200 kHz. For such high current levels and above these frequencies the existing traceable measurement methods are not able to characterize current shunts and cannot provide the phase and magnitude of impedance simultaneously. This paper briefly describes a new broadband method for measuring current shunt standards beyond 1 A in the megahertz region and presents experimental results demonstrating the efficiency of this approach.

articleTitle: Measuring of Electrical Resistivity on NdFeB Magnets Using the Van-Der-Pauw (VDP) Method
abstract: The van-der-Pauw (VDP) method is used to measure the electrical resistivity of NdFeB magnets. The magnet fixture is built and the different grades of NdFeB magnets are measured. The electrical resistivity range of NdFeB is between 1.2 μΩ·m and 1.5μΩ·m. The relative standard deviation of 10 times measurement is 0.18%.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Automated Potentiometer Using a Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: We report the results of a comparison of DC voltage measurements between an automated potentiometer based on a binary voltage divider (BVD) and a programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS). The measurements were carried out at voltages from 10mV to 10 V. BVD was linearized by the self-calibration function of the potentiometer, and the potentiometer was standardized at 10-V level using a Zener standard calibrated with PJVS. The results showed that the relative differences of the measured values are 0.02 μV/V, 0.1 μV/V, and 1.5 μV/V at 10 V, 1 V, and 100 mV, respectively.

articleTitle: New Silicon Crystals for a Redefined Kilogram and Mole: Isotopic Composition of the First Two Crystals
abstract: The isotopic compositions (molar mass, M) of the first and new silicon crystals highly enriched in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si (> 99.99 %) used for the determination of the Avogadro constant were measured using a high resolution multicollector ICP mass spectrometer and applying a modified isotope dilution mass spectrometry technique. Relative uncertainties u<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rel</sub>(M) <; 1 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> were obtained: a reduction by almost three orders of magnitude in ten years. This study compares the homogeneities in M(Si) of the first “AVO28” crystal and the first crystal (Si28-23Pr11) of the “Kilogram-2” project.

articleTitle: Increasing Quantized Single-Electron Current Accuracy in a Tunable Barrier Pump by Two-Gate Modulation
abstract: Tunable barrier single-electron pumps (SEPs) have recently shown their great potential as high precision current source with direct link to the electron charge. The quantization of SEPs realized in gallium-arsenide semiconductors and driven by a single alternating control voltage routinely shows sub-ppm accuracy when applying high magnetic field. However, their accuracy without field is presently much lower. We now have found that modulation of two gates can increase accuracy in zero magnetic field and have confirmed the current quantization I=ef for a frequency of 84.5 MHz within the measurement uncertainty of less than 1 ppm.

articleTitle: Small Force Measurement at CMS/ITRI
abstract: This paper introduces the small force measurement system at micronewton level at Center for Measurement Standards, Industrial Technology Research Institute (CMS/ITRI). The construction of the system started in 2009 and completed in 2014. The force measurement system consists of three main parts: a monolithic flexure stage, a three planar electrodes capacitor and a digital controller. The three planar electrodes capacitor is utilized simultaneously as a position sensor and an electrostatic force generator. Accurate electrostatic force is generated by constantly adjusting and maintaining gap distances between three planar electrodes. The lowest force uncertainty was evaluated to be 4.7 nN. The previous results show that the relative standard uncertainty at 10 μN and 100 μN are 2.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> and 7.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>, respectively. At current stage, the mass of mg level realized by this system has a slightly larger uncertainty than that obtained from traditional subdivision method. We discuss future works to further improve this system.

articleTitle: Electrical Equivalent Loads of an End-Cap Ion-Trap
abstract: The resonant frequency of a helical resonator, that efficiently delivers high voltage rf to an electrodynamic ion-trap, depends on capacitive and inductive loads. Estimation of these loads for the parts that are attached to the resonator are thus necessary for designing a resonator operating at a desired frequency. On the other hand, the trapped ion experiences a voltage induced by the capacitance resulting from the electrodes. This results to excess micromotion to the ion. Here, we estimate the capacitive and resistive loads arising from different parts of ourtrap.

articleTitle: Development of a Shunt for High Intensity DC and AC Currents with NMR Measurement of the Magnetic Field
abstract: This paper describes the development of a new design of a DC and AC shunt to high intensity current. The working principle is based on the measurement of the magnetic field using a nuclear magnetic ressonance or a NMR method. The traceability comes only from frequency and a geometric parameter. The preliminary results of a prototype are presented. Also, it is described a new non-inductive method to measure the magnetic AC component. The final device - a shunt to be used as a primary standard - is intended to operate in kA range.

articleTitle: Double-Modulation Coherent Population Trapping Clock
abstract: Atomic clocks based on coherent population trapping and constructive polarization modulation are promising for high performance and compact devices. We have demonstrated a cw mode CPT clock with a short-term fractional frequency stability at the level of 3. \pmb2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup>/√{τ} for a few 100 s integration time. This Double-Modulation CPT technology can be reduced to a miniature and robust setup due to its linear architecture. This clock could find future applications in industry, telecommunications, instrumentation, or global navigation satellite systems.

articleTitle: Niobium Nano-SQUIDs for Inductive Superconducting Transition Edge Detectors
abstract: Nano-SQUIDs which can be the readout for inductive superconducting transition edge detectors (ISTED) were fabricated on monolayer niobium (Nb) film by focus ion beam (FIB) milling. The dimension of the nanobridges which formed the junctions was less than 60 nm and the diameter of the loop was 20 μm, The properties of this nano-SQUID were investigated. The design of ISTED was introduced and the transition temperature (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) of the absorbing layer was adjusted by both the thickness and the proportion Si doping of Nb.

articleTitle: Volume Measurement of two Spheres from the new Avogadro Crystal Si28-24Pr11
abstract: PTB has again produced a new <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si-crystal (Si28-24Prll) and from that two new spheres. Recently two spheres from the first PTB crystal (Si28-23Prll) had been measured and their results had been used for the special CODATA fixing of Avogadro and Planck constant in the revised International System of Units (SI). Unfortunately, this latest result showed a small deviation from former results (namely of the IAC crystal Si28-10Prll), however, with a reduced uncertainty. Also for the reason to clarify an unknown dependence on the silicon crystal the measurements of this third crystal were performed with priority.

articleTitle: Coherent Control of Acoustic-Wave-Induced Magnetization Dynamics in Magnetic Tunnel Junctions
abstract: We report time-domain measurements of acoustic-wave-induced magnetization dynamics in magnetic tunnel junctions. The acoustic pulses are generated by femtosecond laser excitation and interact with the magnetization through magnetoelastic coupling. The induced magnetization precession is not only dependent on the externally applied magnetic field, but also on the laser excitation position. The presented method even allows us to coherently control the precession using two laser pulses at various magnetic fields and excitation positions.

articleTitle: Design of Digitized Control and Zero Boil-Off Cryogenic Container for CCC inNIM
abstract: As a key instrument for resistance metrology, cryogenic current comparator (CCC) is now widely used in national labs. In order to further improve the performances of CCC and make it easy operate, NIM has made some improvements, which are developing digital controller to replace conventional analog circuit and designing a zero boil-off cryogenic container specially served for CCC. Pre-experiments show that the new digital controller performs a better operability and the zero boil-off cryogenic container has a significant convenience for CCC cryo maintenance.

articleTitle: The Role of the Magnetic Constant, j.10, in the Redefinition of the SI
abstract: This paper explores the origins of the `magnetic constant', \pmbμ0, within the present SI, and its role in the imminent redefinition. An attention to the history and meaning of this constant helps to clarify the structure of our unit system, and reveals the extent to which practical unit choices in electricity influence the way we write the fundamental equations of physics. A concern is raised about the use of the name `vacuum magnetic permeability', as this suggests a physical meaning that is not justified. The potential for misinterpretation will increase when \pmbμ0 becomes experimentally determined in the revised SI.

articleTitle: Harmonic Mitigation of an Improved High Voltage Current Source for On-Site System Calibration of High Voltage Transformer Loss Measurement Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an open-loop technique that mitigates the harmonic distortion in high load currents for onsite system calibrations of high voltage transformer loss measurement systems. The harmonic distortion induced by the current transconductance amplifier and current injector poses high burden on the feedback current correction loop and thus may compromise the measurement accuracy. Accordingly, a harmonic mitigation technique is introduced through online system identification and open-loop anti-harmonic injection. This methodology significantly reduces the THD in the load current from 0.3% to less than 0.022%.

articleTitle: From Electron Pumps to Spin Quantum Bits in Silicon
abstract: Motivated by electrical quantum metrology of the ampere we have developed versatile silicon CMOS based single-electron transistors and quantum dots. Besides charge quantization we can also control the spin degree of freedom of a single holes or electrons confined in those dots. Spin resonance has been observed in both cases although it was less expected for electrons. Furthermore we demonstrated the first spin hole quantum bit in CMOS technology, which offers exciting prospects most notably for scaling as its control is purely electrical thanks to spin-orbit interaction.

articleTitle: High-Precision Mid-IR Molecular Spectroscopy with Traceability to Primary Standards
abstract: We are stabilizing the frequency of a mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) to an optical frequency comb itself stabilized to an ultra-stable near-infrared reference signal at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pmb{1.5\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> transferred from SYRTE to LPL using an optical link. The reference stability is copied to the QCL and we benefit from the traceability to the primary standards of SYRTE. The stabilized QCL can be scanned by scanning the near-IR reference with an electro-optic modulator. We use this ultrastable spectrometer to carry out saturated absorption spectroscopy of methanol. A detailed analysis of the frequency measurement uncertainty will be presented.

articleTitle: Weighing and Moving Mode Experiments in the KRISS Kibble Balance
