abstract: KRISS Kibble balance was successfully set up and weighing and moving mode experiments were performed. The repeatability of weighing mode experiment, (B · l)stat, is about 3 ×10-7. In moving mode, (B · l)dyn, was also evaluated with the region of 2.5 ×10-4 over 10 mm range. Planck constant value will be measured through additional experiments.

articleTitle: GRACE: Developing Electrical Characterisation Methods for Future Graphene Electronics
abstract: GRACE - Developing electrical characterisation methods for future graphene electronics is a 2016 Normative Joint Research Project of the European Metrology Programme for Innovation and Research. The project focuses on the measurement of the electrical properties of graphene. Its objectives are to develop validated measurement methods and protocols, including fast-throughput examples. The work is performed in collaboration with international standardisation committees, with an aim to initiate and develop dedicated documentary standards.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of One-Stream Beamforming System
abstract: This paper presents a one-stream beamforming system based on lx8 high-efficiency patch antenna array and programmable phase shifters with step size 1° and adjustment accuracy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1.5^{\circ}$</tex> typical. The system's E-plane beams with phase differences <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pmb{0^{\circ}, \pm 30^{\circ}, \pm 60^{\circ}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 100^{\circ}$</tex> are measured respectively in the anechoic chamber. It is found that the measured beams are well agreed with the simulated beams: the differences of orientation of main lobe and half power beamwidth are both no more than 1 degree.

articleTitle: Evaluation of JIG Calibration Method for Absorbing Clamp Calibration According to CISPR 16-1-3
abstract: This paper describes JIG method calibration technique for absorbing clamp calibration according to the standard CISPR 16-1-3. Calibration JIG geometrical construction, calibration configuration and its influence to the Clamp Factor (CF) calibration is described.

articleTitle: Development of Power Frequency Digital Phase Shifter
abstract: In the measurement of high voltage loss, a voltage signal and a current signal which were nearly orthogonal to each other need to be measured accurately. If the phase of the voltage signal was shifted by 90° accurately, thus the phase angle between the voltage and the current would be nearly 0°. The two signals would be then easily to measure accurately together. A digital phase shifter was developed. The phase and the magnitude error of the digital phase shifter is less than 6 μrad and 110×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> up to 150 Hz and 120 V, respectively.

articleTitle: Active Guarded Wheatstone Bridge for High Resistance Measurements Up to 100 TΩ at TÜBİTAK UME
abstract: We present an active guarded Wheatstone bridge, developed at TÜBİTAK UME, for high resistance measurements between \pmb100 M\pmbΩ to \pmb100 T\pmbΩ up to 1000 V. The guarded box connections and special low noise cables were used to reduce noise and leakage currents causing measurement errors. This has enabled us to perform stable measurements at higher resistor values.

articleTitle: Observation of High Accuracy Resistance Quantization in CVD Graphene
abstract: A prime technique to produce graphene is Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD). In this paper, the first observation of high accuracy resistance quantization in CVD graphene samples grown on polycrystalline copper foils is shown. High precision measurements performed using a cryogenic current comparator reveal a resistance quantization accuracy of 100 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>.

Author Keywords: Quantum Hall Effect (QHE) and Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC)

articleTitle: Optical Frequency Measurements at 1×10−18 Uncertainty with Ytterbium Optical Lattice Clocks
abstract: We describe ytterbium optical lattice clocks under development at NIST. This includes the characterization of optical frequency stability and uncertainty, as well as measurements between two independent clocks, at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−18</sup>level. We also report on optical frequency ratio measurements with other optical clocks at NIST.

articleTitle: The Kibble Balance and the Forthcoming Revision of the SI
abstract: The redefinition of the kilogram in the forthcoming revision of the SI has been strongly supported by the many instruments which use the Kibble virtual work technique. For the forthcoming revision of the SI the instruments measured the value of the Planck constant in SI units; after the revision these, and additional instruments, will be used to maintain the world's mass scale. This paper provides a short description of the measurements which have been made to support the redefinition of the kilogram, the existing instruments which utilise the Kibble technique and the possible evolution of the technique after redefinition.

articleTitle: Development of New Standard Resistors
abstract: Precision resistance metrology requires standard resistors with excellent stability in order to maintain the level of uncertainty achieved by quantum standards such as the quantum Hall effect. Stable 10 kΩ resistors are in particularly high demand for maintenance purposes and as a starting point for improved scaling to high resistance values above 1 MΩ. Recently, PTB has started a cooperation project with an industrial partner to develop new standard resistors. This work presents the first results of new types of 10 kΩ resistors. Stability of less than 0.5 μΩ/Ω per year has already been realized.

articleTitle: Supplementary Comparison EURAMET.EM-S31
abstract: Within the framework of the Supplementary Comparison EURAMET.EM-S31, the capacitance derived from the quantized Hall resistance at either ac or dc as well as the 10:1 capacitance ratio was intercompared. In addition, the frequency dependence of two traveling AC-DC resistors was intercompared to test the AC-DC resistance standards involved in the particular capacitance realizations. At the end, a good agreement was achieved for all measurands by all participants. By virtue of a link to the NMIA calculable cross-capacitor, a value of the von Klitzing constant in agreement with the 2014 CODATA value was determined.

articleTitle: REFIMEVE+: Towards a Wide Optical Fiber Network for Optical Frequency Standard Dissemination
abstract: We report on the progress of a metrological fiber network on the French territory, with extensiONS to Europe, which aims to provide an ultra-stable frequency signal to around 20 laboratories. We present a low sensitivity multi-branch Michelson interferometer serving as a node for the dissemination to several network branches. We show in addition reliable and robust operation over several months of operation of a 1400 km, which instability is in the - 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-20</sup> range at long-term. This work is an important step towards the realization of an effective fiber network disseminating optical frequency standards to a wide variety of research laboratories.

articleTitle: Calibration of Gain Ratios on nV-Meters with the Reference Step Method
abstract: The Reference Step Method for calibrators can be modified for calibration also of the gain ratios on a meter. The method has earlier been evaluated in the range 100 mV - 1000 V on DMM HP 3458A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> and shows that an accuracy of typically could be obtained. We have investigated the performance of the method when calibrating ratios in the range 1 mV - 100 mV on two common nV-meters. In our comparisons with the Josephson Voltage Standard the differences are within \pmb± 12μ V/V at the ratio 10m V:1mV and within \pmb±1.3μ V/V at 100mV:10mV.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Measure γHe/γXe
abstract: A novel technique to extract the quotient of gyromagnetic ratios in a comagnetometer system is presented. This technique aims to probe the quotient in a regime which is free from the spin-relaxation related systematic effects. It is based on the measurement of spin precession frequencies in a gaseous mixture of 129Xe and<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>He at ultralow magnetic field. The resultant quotient value appears to be close to the literature value.

articleTitle: Characterization of 1 Ω, 10 Ω and 1 kΩ Metal-Foil Standard Resistors
abstract: We have been developing and evaluating metal-foil standard resistors manufactured based on the Stress Free Bulk Metal Foil technology. This paper describes drift characterization of 1 kΩ standard resistors and continuing long-term drift characterization of 1 Ω, 10 Ω standard resistors. We found that all resistors show extremely small drift rates., e.g., 5 nΩ/(Ω year) for 1 kΩ standard resistors.

articleTitle: Evaluation Standard Uncertainty Depends on Travelling Standard Instability During Key Comparison
abstract: This paper deals with some problems concerning the evaluation of standard uncertainty depends on travelling standard instability and its further influence on evaluation uncertainty of key comparison reference value during a key comparison of national standards. The authors have proposed an explicit practical approach for evaluating standard uncertainty depends on travelling standard instability when the radial scheme of comparisons is used. As an example, the approach is applied to key comparison COOMET.EM-K5.

articleTitle: Improved S-Parameter Measurements of Embedded Planar Transmission-Line on Multi-Layer PCB
abstract: This paper describes improved calibration method for measuring the scattering parameters of an embedded planar transmission line on multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB) substrate from 100 MHz to 40 GHz. When using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) to measure the scattering parameters (S-parameters) of printed circuit board (PCB) interconnects, it can be advantageous to include the calibration and verification standards on the same PCB as the interconnects under test. Both designs of on-PCB standards and calibrated results of verification standards are presented.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of a Capacitive Sensor with a Grounded Shield Window
abstract: Theoretical analysis of a differential capacitive sensor with a grounded shield window is presented in this paper. The analysis is based on the conformal transformation. It has been theoretically proven that this sensor is sensitive to the motion with only one translational degree of freedom (DOF), and immune to the vibration along the other two translational DOFs.

articleTitle: Metrological Traceability of Scattering Parameter Up to 18 GHz for BNC 75–Ω Connector
abstract: This paper presents the achievement of primary scattering parameter (S-parameter) measurement standard based on the precision coaxial air lines with BNC, 75 ohms connectors. The primary standard can as a reference to calibrate a device under test up to 18 GHz. The mechanical measurements of the line's diameters and length made accurately using NMIJ's standard system. Furthermore, the small insertion loss also measured in the microwave frequency regions. The established primary standard is the first achievement to undertake the traceability of S-parameter measurement up to 18 GHz in the author's knowledge.

articleTitle: N Anoscale Magnetometry Using Single Spin Quantum Sensors
abstract: Advancing the frontiers of nanoscience and information technology hinges on the availability of novel tools for nanoscale sensing and imaging. Solid-state electronic spins offer a unique platform to implement high-performance quantum sensing devices, which address this need and go beyond what classical technologies offer. We present a robust technology to realise this concept, which is based on nano-engineered diamond devices, hosting single electronic spins for sensing. We will describe the key principles underlying these novel quantum sensors and discuss some of their areas of applications which we have opened over the last years. These include the field of antiferromagnetic spintronics, where single spin magnetometry already yields unprecedented insight into domain formation and non-trivial spin-textures in antiferromagnets. Next to these room-temperature applications, we will present results of cryogenic single spin magnetometry for quantitative, high resolution imaging of vortices and supercurrents in nanoscale superconductors. These examples illustrate the remarkable performance that single spin quantum sensing offers, and which holds great promise for future applications in various applicatons of the nano-sciences.

articleTitle: Precise Determination of the Ratio h/mu: A Way to Link Microscopic Mass to the New Kilogram
abstract: The ratio h/mu between the Planck constant and the unified atomic mass constant should have a special status in the framework of the future International System of Units. As the Planck constant h will be fixed, the ratio h/mu will ensure the realization of the new kilogram (quantum kilogram) at the atomic scale. Furthermore, this ratio becomes a key data for the realization of the kilogram at the macroscopic scale using the XRCD method. The ratio h/mu can be precisely determined from the measurement of the atomic recoil due to the absorption of a photon momentum. In this conference we will present the lastest developments of our experiment in Paris that aims to measure precisely the recoil of rubidium atom using atom interferometry.

articleTitle: Compact Distributed Digitizers with Metrological Precision
abstract: Prototype distributed digitizers have been developed with metrological precision of the individual measurement nodes. A master controller aggregates the data of the nodes and performs all computational tasks. A crucial part of the system is the synchronization of the individual nodes at nanosecond level using white-rabbit technology. Fibre-optic communication is used to reduce interference and to obtain high isolation. When operated on battery power, this allows for special applications such as the measurement of currents in high-voltage lines. First results show that a phase difference between nodes of a few μrad can be achieved with a resolution of better than 0.1 μrad.

articleTitle: Comparison of VoltRef and New CMI Software for Zener Standards Maintenance
abstract: A new software tool for intercomparison of a group of Zener reference standards has been developed. It was tested together with the commonly used software VoltRef and results show significant improvement in measured values. The new software also overcomes limitations of the VotlRef and gives user a larger control over the measurement method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Correlation in the Intercomparison of DC Voltage Reference Standards
abstract: This paper describes the application of GUM Supplement 1 and Supplement 2 in the intercomparison procedure of a group of four DC voltage reference standards. The results obtained are presented and the influence of the correlation on the estimation of the voltage values is analyzed.

articleTitle: Accurate Measurement at the Nanoscale of Remnant Polarisation Charge in Ferroelectric Films
abstract: A method for the measurement of the remnant polarisation charge of ferroelectric films at the nanoscale is proposed. It is based on current measurement by an atomic force microscope and imposes a capacitive correction in order to extract the signal from the noise, several orders of magnitude higher than the signal to be measured. A remnant charge of 4.2 fC could be measured on a PbZrTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>thin film. Solutions to decrease the noise are proposed.

articleTitle: Progress in Fluxgate Current Transducers
abstract: This paper describes recent technological progress in the field of high accuracy fluxgate current transducers. After an introduction into the subject, followed by advantages and limitations, innovative waveforms for fluxgate excitation and their digital signal processing are described in more detail, followed by an explanation of key performance parameters of a new product.

articleTitle: Spin Hall Effect Device for Magnetic Sensor Application
abstract: In this paper, the spin Hall device was fabricated to magnetic sensor applications. This device based on the spin Hall effect by observing in ferromagnetic and heavy metal multi-layer structures. We measured shift of switching current with changing a z-component of small magnetic field through anomalous Hall effect measurement. The shift of switching current can be applied the magnetic sensor. Also, we controlled the sensitivity of this device changing efficiency of spin Hall effect. This device is a good candidate for magnetic sensor to measure a wide dynamic range of magnetic field.

articleTitle: Implementation of Certified 150–Ω Voltage Probe for IEC 61967–4 Conducted Electromagnetic Emission Measurement
abstract: A 150-Ω probe which fully complied with the IEC standard 61967-4 is proposed for the conducted emission testing at IC level. The 150-Ω direct coupling method is reviewed, and the concern of precise measurement and the property of easy to use is discussed. The 150-Ω network is implemented by the integrated passive device (IPD) process instead of surface-mount devices (SMDs). With the reduced parasitic effect, the proposed 150-Ω probe is verified to fulfill the specifications of IEC standard which make the characterization of EMI at IC level guarantee the high precision and high repeatability.

articleTitle: Nano - Microscale Electrical Characterization of Copper Thru Silicon Vias in 3D Stacked Integrated Circuits
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of different electrical measurements techniques and systems operating at nano and micro scales for the electrical characterization of copper filled Thru Silicon Vias used for 3D integrated circuits interconnects and defect detection in such vias.

articleTitle: Tattoo Inks EM Characterization for MRI Interaction Evaluation
abstract: The lack of knowledge about the safety implications of tattooed individuals subjected to Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) may, sometimes, lead to an exaggerate reaction from physicians such as the avoidance of the exam for tattooed patients. To explore the actual risks, in this work, the magnetic and electrical properties of five different tattoo inks have been measured to investigate their interaction with the MRI electromagnetic (EM) fields. Results highlight that the magnetic and electrical behaviour strongly depend on the type of analyzed ink. Magnetic measurements also reveal a different response between the ink solutions and the relative pigments.

articleTitle: Inductance Imitator Instead of Toroidal Coil?
abstract: Three inductance imitator models of 100 mH being four-terminal networks with 4TP definition were developed. The devices are suitable for shipment by any means of transport. Main characteristics of the imitators were compared with those of 100-mH inductance standard EI-2 (analogue of GR1482-L) from VNIIM group standard. The experimental results confirm feasibility of 100-mH inductance standard comparisons by using the inductance imitators instead of the commonly used standards with toroidal windings.

articleTitle: Calibration of Multi-Tone Stimulus Harmonic Phase Reference Based on DRTO and Prime Number Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposed a prime number algorithm to avoid embedded errors when using Digital Real-Time Oscilloscope to calibrate a multi-tone stimulus harmonic phase reference. Measurement results are presented to verify the validity of the frequency selection algorithms.

articleTitle: Measurement of Radio-Frequency Radiation Pressure
abstract: In this work we perform measurements of the radiation pressure of a radio-frequency (RF) electromagnetic field which will lead to a new SI traceable power calibration. There are several groups around the world investigating methods to perform more direct SI traceable measurement of RF power (where RF is defined to range from 100s of MHz to THz). A measurement of radiation pressure offers the possibility for a measure traceable to the kilogram and to Planck's constant through the redefined SI. Towards this goal, we demonstrate the ability to measure the radiation pressure/force carried in a field at 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Phase Measurement Performance Evaluation of Differential Sampling System
abstract: In this paper, we introduced a method to measure AC power. Here, phase measurement performance was evaluated from the following perspectives as zero phase and different angle stability, small angle accuracy. The results shown that the diffderential sampling system has a high accuracy, where the variety of zero is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\ \mu \mathrm{rad}$</tex> in four days, the difference between differential sampling system and lock-in amplifier on small angle phase measurement is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\ \mu \mathrm{rad}$</tex>, and the differential sampling system has a good stability in different angle phase measurement.

articleTitle: Towards High Frequency Power Measurement Using the Electro-Optical Effect
abstract: This paper describes experimental measurements for high frequency power with a Mach-Zehnder modulator. The interest of using the electro-optic effect for high frequency power measurements is that measurements can be done very fast compared to calorimeter measurements. The tested linearity range of the Mach-Zehnder interferometer is between 6 dBm and 18 dBm at frequencies from 1 MHz to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Measurement of G with Angular Acceleration Feedback Method
abstract: The large spread in recent published G values suggests that there may be some undiscovered systematic sources in these experiments. With the aim of identifying possible errors and obtaining a more reliable G value, our group has performed two independent methods simultaneously. Besides the time-of-swing method which we have worked on for more than 20 years [1], [2], another determination of G with the angular acceleration feedback method was carried out at the same laboratory. In the AAF method, two coaxial turntables are used to rotate the torsion pendulum and the source masses individually. With the help of a feedback control system [3], the torsion fiber does not twist by matching the rotating rate of the two turntables. As a result, this method is insensitive to the fiber's properties. In this work, several sources of uncertainty existed in our preliminary experiment [4] are reduced: (1) An ultra-low thermal expansion (ULE) glass shelfis used to support the source masses instead of the aluminium shelf to reduce the temperature influence on the distance between source masses; (2) The background gravity gradient of the rotating shelf is measured and compensated with small blocks so that its effect to the G value is reduced to ~1 ppm; (3) Two different methods are used to check the source mass distance to improve the confidence level. With the improvements shown above and a lot of careful systematic error evaluation, a new G value with a prospective uncertainty of less than 15 ppm will be obtained.

articleTitle: Experiments to Extend the Retrace Specification of Fluke Zener Reference Standards
abstract: Fluke zener reference standards were designed to operate under constant power, whether it is from line power or from the batteries. Fluke has a published specification associated with the loss of power to the device under laboratory conditions for up to 24 hours (Retrace). Fluke has performed research and development on a new generation of Zener Reference standards, and as part of the research, experiments were conducted to quantify the uncertainty associated with removing power to the units for extended periods of time. The results of the experiment are presented, with interpretation of the data.

articleTitle: Absolute Terahertz Power Measurement of Tens of Nanowatts Using a Highly-Sensitive Calorimeter at Room Temperature
abstract: This study demonstrates a quantitative measurement of absolute terahertz power of tens of nanowatts at room temperature. A highly sensitive calorimetric measurement system is constructed using an extremely low noise amplifier and multilayer thermal insulation jackets. A vacuum insulator is used to mitigate thermal disturbance; therefore, very stable measurements are realized at room temperature. As a result, the absolute power of 26.7 nW is measured at 1 THz with the relative expanded uncertainty of 4.2% (k=2).

articleTitle: Evaluation of Deterioration Degree of Electrical Contacts with Precise Impedance Measurement
abstract: Deterioration processes of tin-plated base metal contacts are caused by complex factors. Many connectors with ongoing deterioration are in the danger of becoming defective suddenly. In most cases, the change of contact resistance of connectors during those deterioration processes doesn't monotonically increase, that makes it difficult to evaluate the degree of deterioration with resistance measurement. It is observed that the changes in reactance at a certain frequency behave characteristically and independently of the resistance changes. It is possible to estimate the deterioration degree from the precise AC measurements because the change reflects the microstructural changes near contacts.

articleTitle: Quantum Hall Resistance Verification Based on a Direct Current Comparator Bridge
abstract: We describe measurements using a quantum Hall system equipped with a liquefier and a room temperature direct current comparator bridge to transfer the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k-90</sub>/2 value of 12906.4035 Ω to a 1 kΩ. Subsequently we scale from the 1 kΩ down to the 1 Ω to an uncertainty of 0.02 ppm. Estimates of the relative uncertainties of the quantum Hall effective are compared to the estimates of the older wet quantum Hall effective along with scaling methods will be provided in this report and a discussion of the advantages of the scaling paths.

articleTitle: New Setup for Bridge Amplifier Linearity Investigation
abstract: We present a setup for linearity investigation of high precision bridge amplifiers as used for strain gauge transducer in static force and torque measurements. The setup allows to characterize bridge amplifiers in much more detail than the 0.1m V/V step size of the BN100 bridge standard or a recently proposed resistor-based strain gauge bridge transducer simulator. Only with the presented linearity investigation setup it is now possible to verify the specified uncertainty of high precision bridge amplifiers of \pmb5. 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>mV/V at 225 Hz.

articleTitle: Calibration Factor Measurement up to 50 GHz at TÜBİTAK UME
abstract: TUBİTAK UME has established a new power sensor calibration setup incorporating a monitor power sensor utilizing the direct comparison transfer method for frequencies up to 50 GHz. The system adds to TÜBİTAK UME's existing capability to measure power sensors with type Nand 3.5 mm connectors. The new measurement setup was validated using certificate values of power sensors for each working frequency range. Good agreement was found between previous calibration results and those obtained with the new system.

articleTitle: Terahertz Metrology at PTB
abstract: Terahertz (THz) metrology is performed at the THz radiometry working group of PTB by offering a unique calibration service of the THz power responsivity of suitable detectors in the spectral range from 0.7 THz to 5 THz. A molecular gas laser enables a calibration uncertainty of which was proven by a pilot comparison between the metrology institutes of China, USA and Germany. Usually, the THz power scale is disseminated by novel pyroelectric thin-film detectors. Moreover, these detectors can be applied as a reference material to check the precision of transmission and reflection measurements in the far-infrared to sub-millimeter range.

articleTitle: Study on the phase shifter in josephson junctions embedded microwave circuits
abstract: In a programmable Josephson voltage standard device which contains multiple branches of Josephson junction (JJ) array, the microwave reflection in arrays may result in a decrease in the Shapiro step margin. According to most of the previous designs, 90° phase shifter is used to cancel microwave reflection from branches to improve the performance of the device. This paper reports our study of the phase shifter in JJ array device with a 2-stage Wilkinson power divider. At first we designed and fabricated JJ array circuits with the phase shifters. Measurement results indicate that unequal powers have been reached to arrays. We then deleted the phase shifters in another design. Identical Shapiro step margins for 4 JJ array branches are achieved.

articleTitle: An AC Four-Terminal Low Value Resistance Bridge
abstract: This paper describes a current transformer based ac four-terminal low value resistance measurement bridge. The design and performance of this bridge is presented, which compares resistors from 10 to 0.1 ohm over a frequency range of 100 Hz-10kHz. The reference ratio arm used in this bridge is a special designed high accurate zero-flux current transformer (ZFCT). The current ratio value of the ZFCT is self-calibrated by using the conventional build up method. An auxiliary current transformer combined with variable impedance is used to constitute the wagner circuit.

articleTitle: Construction of Maxwell-Wien Bridge at SASO-NMCC
abstract: An inductance calibration system for standard inductors based on a Maxwell-Wien bridge has been constructed at Saudi Standards Metrology and Quality Organization, National Measurement and Calibration Center (SASO NMCC). Expanded measurement uncertainty has been estimated to be less than \pmb20 μH/H for 100 mH inductance at 1 kHz. A bilateral comparison between SASO NMCC and TÜBİTAK UME has been performed in order to evaluate the performance of the calibration system.

articleTitle: Epitaxial Graphene p-n Junctions
abstract: We report the fabrication and measurement of top gated epitaxial graphene p-n junctions where exfoliated hexgonal boron nitride (hBN) is used as the gate dielectric. The four terminal longitudinal resistance across a single junction is well quantized at R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K -90</sub>(=25812.807 Ω) with a relative uncertainty of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>. Our work opens the possibility to realize programmable electrical resistance standards using external gating.

articleTitle: Quantum Imaging with Photon-Number Correlations
abstract: Non-classical correlations in optical beams offer the unprecedented opportunity of surpassing conventional limits of sensitivity and resolution in optical measurements and imaging, especially but not only, when a low photon flux down/single photons are measured. We review the principles quantum imaging and sensing techniques presenting some state-of-the-art achievements in the field. These quantum protocols have the potential to trigger major steps in many application ranging from radiometry to biophotonics.

articleTitle: Purpose-Built Air Bath for use with NMIA Calculable Cross-Capacitor Measurement Chain
abstract: This paper describes the design of an air bath for maintaining the reference capacitors associated with the new NMIA calculable cross-capacitor measurement system. The air bath is designed to maintain a set temperature in the range 15°C to 25 °C with a stability of 0.1 mK over the short time periods during which the capacitors are measured.

articleTitle: An Improved Round Robin Device for ILCs on Harmonics Between EMC Testing Laboratories
abstract: A patent-pending device designed as a round robin test device for inter-laboratory comparisons (ILCs) between EMC testing laboratories in the field of harmonic emissions is described. Its advanced features in generating and monitoring current harmonics are explained. And, its adaptivity to the mains frequency is analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Note on Handling Source Mismatch in RF Power Measurement and Metrology
abstract: This paper presents an analytic study of reducing the contribution of source mismatch in RF power measurements. With implementation of a two-port network (i.e., an attenuator) in between a RF source and a load (e.g., a power sensor), the contribution of source mismatch could be substituted by the reflection coefficient of the attenuator at its port connected with the load, if its attenuation value is high. In the paper, performance of the method has also been successfully evaluated and discussed with different scenarios.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Rydberg Constant with Trapped Rydberg Atoms
abstract: A measurement of the Rydberg constant using cold circular Rydberg atoms is proposed. Since these atoms have long lifetimes, negligible quantum electrodynamics and no nuclear-overlap corrections, the measurement can shed new light on the “proton radius puzzle”. The atoms are trapped in an optical lattice. Transitions are driven using a lattice-modulation technique to perform Doppler-free sub-THz spectroscopy; the transition frequencies yield the Rydberg constant. The selected transitions are free of first-order Zeeman and Stark shifts. Systematic uncertainties due to lattice-induced shifts, core-polarization, second-order Zeeman and Stark shifts, etc are estimated.

articleTitle: Reference Ultra Low DC Current Source (ULCS) Between 1 fA and 100pA at TÜBİ:TAK UME
abstract: We present a programmable ultra low DC current source (ULCS), developed at TÜBITAK UME, from 1 fA up to 100 pA with 100 aA resolution. The principle of the device is based on applying a ramp voltage on standard capacitors with values between 1 pF and 1000 pF. The standard capacitors are kept in a temperature controlled box. The device is fully automated with computer control and can be used to generate any currents with 100 aA resolution in its range.

articleTitle: Practical Application of Optimal Hollow Active Auxiliary Electrode in Vertical Calculable Capacitor at NIM
abstract: After the continual investigation on the electrical compensation method for the end effect, the optimal hollow active auxiliary electrode (OHAAE) has been successfully developed and substituted for the current nosepiece in the new vertical calculable capacitor (CC) at NIM. Applying the best compensation voltage of Ubest obtained from the model tests, the initial measurement result by the OHAAE in the new vertical CC for reproducing the 1 pF capacitance of the same commercial capacitor agrees with that by the nosepiece in the level of 6.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>.

articleTitle: DC Voltage Calibration System Based on the Step Reference Method at CEM
abstract: This paper describes the new calibration system for DC Voltage at the Spanish Center of Metrology based on the Step Reference Method. It's a very flexible implementation of the method, allowing the calibration not only of sources but of high accuracy multimeters.

articleTitle: Study of Accuracy and Stability of Sr Lattice Clocks at LNE-SYRTE
abstract: In this paper, we describe the operation of two optical lattice clocks operated at LNE-SYRTE. They feature an accuracy down to 2.1 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-17</sup>, and each clock has a fractional frequency stability of 7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup>/√(τ). We propose the updated accuracy budget of these clocks, with specific evaluations of the lattice-induced effect, as well as the characterization of a spurious systematic effect due to electric cross-talk between the clocks cycle and the clock laser that was recently observed. Reliably operating these two clocks led to the first contribution of an optical clock to TAI. Finally, we report on a non-destructive detection scheme aiming at improving the clock stability.

articleTitle: Theoretical Basis of a High Frequency Matching Approach to Calibrate Current Shunt Standards up to 1 MHz
abstract: Wideband current shunts are usually used in national metrology institutes to perform AC current measurements. Actually, current shunt standards are commonly calibrated up to 100 kHz using a low frequency approach. The existing traceable measurement methods to characterize current shunt standards are limited in frequency to 100 kHz for current levels above 10 A. This paper describes a theoretical basis of a new high frequency approach based on the use of an impedance matching circuit and a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). Theoretically, this new method is able to measure and characterize current shunts at frequencies up to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Diffraction Correction of Locking Fabry-Perot Interferometer in Calculable Capacitor at NIM
abstract: This paper describes a diffraction correction of the displacement measurement in calculable capacitor. A mathematical model of the locking interferometer based on Gaussian beam propagation is set up. The phase difference between the two cavities of interest is analyzed numerically. The simulation result demonstrates that the minimum value of the displacement correction can be obtained by actively detecting the laser light at a distance of 560 mm from output mirror.

articleTitle: A Defect Opening Profile Estimation Method Based on the Right-Angle Characteristic of Vertical Component of MFL Signal
abstract: In the magnetic flux leakage (MFL) testing technique, the vertical component of MFL signal contains essential right-angle information of defect, which is useful for the defect profile estimation. This paper analyzes the right-angle characteristic of vertical component of MFL signal, and sums up two types of signal feature for different kinds of right angle. A method based on the vertical component signal feature is also proposed to estimate the defect opening profile. Simulation result validates the well performance for the defect opening profile estimation, especially for the right-angel detection.

articleTitle: Qualifying a Transient Recorder for Traceable Measurements of Very Fast Transients
abstract: This paper presents the qualification of a transient recorder used in a system for traceable measurements of Very Fast Transients. The system is designed for traceable measurements of VFT up to 100 kV, having a target settling time , a peak voltage error , and a front time error . The rise time of the digitizer is 1.6 ns at 50Ω and 1.2 ns at 1 MΩ. Step responses show settling times of 4.5 ns. A convolution method gives a peak voltage error of 0.12% and a front time error of 4.1% for 4.5ns front times.

articleTitle: Spin Caloritronic Measurements: A Round Robin Comparison of the Longitudinal Spin Seebeck Effect
abstract: The rising field of spin caloritronics focuses on the interactions between spin and heat currents in a magnetic material. The observation of the spin Seebeck effect opened the route to this branch of research making possible the design of thermoelectric devices made of insulating magnetic materials. A round robin test performed by five partners on a single device highlighted the reproducibility problems related to the measurements of the spin Seebeck coefficient, the quantity that describes the strength of the spin Seebeck effect. This work stimulated the search for more reproducible measurement methods.

articleTitle: Past and Future of Optical Clocks Toward Redefinition of the Second
abstract: Following the major revision of four SI units in 2018, redefinition of the second based on optical clocks is becoming foreseeable. This presentation briefly shows how optical frequency standards have made progress to surpass microwave frequency standards, and the level they are presently at. The future redefinition also requires the advances in the capability of remote frequency comparison to confirm the frequency reproducibility of standards as well as to maintain International Atomic Time (TAI) compatible with an optical definition. Such issues to be resolved prior to the redefinition are also discussed.

articleTitle: Development of Calibration System for Defibrillator Analyzers
abstract: To ensure the traceability and reliability of the electrical defibrillation pulse energy, this paper presents the development of an integral source-meter setup for the calibration of defibrillator analyzers, that has been designed to generate and measure both typical monophasic and biphasic waveforms. By synchronously sampling the pulse voltage and current to calculate the energy, the 0.2%E+0.1 J uncertainties of pulse energy from 0.1 J to 360 J are achieved and independent of the load.

articleTitle: Calibration of Dissipation Factor Measurements of Capacitance Meters
abstract: A calibration procedure of absolute dissipation factor calibration for commercial capacitance meters has been developed at TÜBİTAK UME between dissipation factor values 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for the frequencies between 60 Hz and 20 kHz. A guard ring capacitor was employed to determine dissipation factor measurement error of capacitance meter at very low values. Resistors of different values are connected series to capacitor in order to obtain desired dissipation factor measurements, for dissipation factor values higher than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>. In this work, AH2500A and AH2700A ultra precision capacitance bridges were employed as capacitance meters.

articleTitle: Influence of Atomic Clock's Frequency Correction to UTC(IMBH) Time Scale Stability
abstract: The aim of steering national time scale of Bosnia and Herzegovina UTC(IMBH) is to keep it accurate and stable. Steering of UTC(IMBH) is realized by applying frequency corrections into atomic clock 5071A on the daily basis. Consequences of frequency correction value to short and long term time scale stability are evaluated. The intention of this work is to find optimal solution between applied relative frequency correction and time scale stability.

articleTitle: Development of Yb Optical Lattice Clock to 10−17 Uncertainty Level and a New Clock Laser System at KRISS
abstract: The systematic uncertainty of the Yb optical lattice clock has been improved to 8.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-17</sup> at KRISS, and the absolute frequency has been measured with uncertainty of 9.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> referenced to the SI second (TT). We also describe future prospects to further reduce the systematic uncertainty and the absolute frequency measurement uncertainty. A new clock laser system has been developed to evaluate the uncertainties in reasonably short time.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of physically-linked large-scale josephson junction test arrays
abstract: The efforts of National Institute of Metrology (NIM) towards large scale Nb/ Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Si1-<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> /Nb Josephson junction arrays for the quantum voltage standards are presented in this paper. Physically-linked arrays with 10,000 and 20,000 junctions (corresponding to 1 and 2 junctions vertically) are fabricated. DC I-V characteristics of different stacked arrays are measured and experimental results are discussed. Focusing ion beam (FIB) together with scanning electron microscope (SEM) are used to examine the cross-section of three types of junction stacks which vertically contains 2, 3, and 4 junctions respectively. It is shown that grain boundary defects in the niobium wiring layer exist for all of these junction stacks. A method which potentially could solve this problem is proposed.

articleTitle: Reassessment of the Uncertainties of the NRC Cryogenic Current Comparator and Quantum Hall Resistance Standard
abstract: This paper describes the main sources of error in the NRC Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC) and Quantum Hall Resistance Standard (QHR) systems and reports their estimated uncertainty. The CCC type B uncertainty is evaluated to be 0.26 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>, with the largest contribution being the effect of a noise-induced offset in the Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID). The relative uncertainty of the QHR system is estimated at 0.28 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>, with comparable contributions from leakage resistances between the leads and finite dissipation on the QHR sample.

articleTitle: Improved Power Coefficient of Sensitivity in a Series-Parallel Circuit of Thermal Converters
abstract: The power coefficient of sensitivity is a useful measure that can provide a deep insight into the improvement of the low-frequency ac-dc transfer difference. We have, therefore, derived the power coefficient of series-parallel connected thermal converters (TC) arranged in an m × m matrix, as a lowfrequency ac-dc transfer standard. The obtained power coefficient of the m × m series-parallel connected TCs is found to decrease proportional to 1/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, without any decrease in the sensitivity. The experimental results are in close agreement with the results of the analysis.

articleTitle: DC Voltage Traceability to Microvolt and Nanovolt Levels
abstract: This paper describes a simple calibration method for nanovoltmeters, that allows the determination and correction of gain errors for the microvolt and nanovolt ranges, giving a real traceability to the low level voltage measurements. The method also permits a realistic estimation of the measurement uncertainty associated to the gain errors of nanovoltmeters that is usually lower than the estimation based on the manufacturer specifications.

articleTitle: Progress Toward Radiation-Pressure-Enabled Traceable Laser Sources
abstract: Radiation pressure has recently been shown to have practical application for multi-kilowatt laser power measurement. One key advantage lies in its ability to measure without absorbing the laser beam. This enables a new measurement paradigm where laser power can be measured traceable to the SI without perturbing the beam. Combining this measurement scheme with a laser constitutes a “traceable source” where laser output power is traceable to the SI in real time. This greatly simplifies the calibration process for multi-kilowatt laser power meters and yields a path to high-accuracy laser-based material processing.

articleTitle: Calibration of Measuring Network of Leakage Current Tester by High Frequency Current Source
abstract: A novel method, which is different from the high frequency voltage source method recommended by IEC 60990, is proposed in this paper. Calibration of the leakage current measuring network is realized by direct current input using high frequency current source. It has been verified that the measurement results consist with the requirements of IEC 60990.

articleTitle: Models for Synchrophasor with Step Discontinuities in Magnitude and Phase, Their Parameter Estimation and Performance
abstract: This work proposes an alternative method to assess the calibration of phasor measurements units (PMUs) under magnitude and phase step conditions. Two parametric mathematical models are used to represent the signal and an iterative numerical method is used to best fit the model parameters to the samples. This approach avoids the adjustment of time windows around the instant of the discontinuity. The estimated parameters can be used to calculate a reference phasor with an appropriate definition.

articleTitle: Real-Time Confocal Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) for Spectroscopic Sensing of Cancer Tissues
abstract: We demonstrated GPU accelerated real-time confocal fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) based on the analog mean-delay (AMD) method. The frame rate of our system was demonstrated to be 13 fps for a 200 × 200 pixel image when observing maize vascular tissue. This system can be utilized for studying spectroscopic characteristics of cancer tissues.

articleTitle: Software Identification for Smart Meters
abstract: Software plays an important role for smart meters. Legal metrology requires that after a type of meters is approved, all the meters of this type should contain exact the same software as the software submitted during type approval. Software identification is the widely used means for software identity checking. This paper lists five methods for software identification, two of which are the existing static methods. In order to overcome the weakness of the static methods, we propose three dynamic methods.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Dual Josephson Impedance Bridge
abstract: This paper describes a dual Josephson impedance bridge capable of comparing any two impedances, that is, with any amplitude ratio and relative phase, over a wide range of frequency. A new, more compact, design has been achieved by mounting the two Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizers (dual JAWS) side-by-side in a single cryoprobe. We measured the crosstalk between the two JAWS sources and show that, by interchanging the impedances within the bridge, the effect of the crosstalk between JAWS sources can be reduced to a negligible level.

articleTitle: The JILA (Parks-Faller) 2010 Determination of the Newtonian Constant
abstract: We present here an update of the JILA (Parks-Faller) 2010 determination of the Newtonian Constant of gravitation (big \pmbG). Due to an Abbe error that was unaccounted for in the initial analysis, we adjust our value of the gravitational constant \pmbG from \pmb(6.67234± 0.00014) ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> to \pmb(6.67296±0.00022)×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. We discuss the source of the error and how it can be avoided in future iterations of this experiment.

articleTitle: Development of AC Quantum Hall Measurements at CMI
abstract: This paper describes results and equipment involved in experiments with realization of quantum impedance standard, based on ac quantum Hall resistance standard. CMI developed cryogenic probe with TO-8 holder and coaxial wiring, device holder and digitally assisted (DA) bridge suitable for ac measurements of quantum Hall effect. Experiments were performed at liquid helium temperatures with GaAs devices placed in double shielded holders.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters up to 100 MHz
abstract: Membrane-supported thin-film multijunction thermal converters on crystalline quartz have been assembled in a high-frequency optimized housing to achieve lowest AC-DC voltage transfer differences. By extensive electromagnetic simulation, special emphasis has been placed on the investigation of the significant influence of chip bonding, housing, and connecting transmissions lines on the overall performance up to 100 MHz.

articleTitle: Traceable Site-VSWR Measurements for Validating Anechoic Chamber
abstract: This paper presents recent works on traceable site-VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio) measurements for validating RF semi-anechoic chamber in 1 GHz - 18 GHz, in accordance with CISPR (International Special Committee on Radio Interference) 16-1-4 technical standard. In this work, site imperfection which is an important contributor for radiated emission measurement uncertainties, have been accurately characterized and discussed using different antenna height and polarization.

articleTitle: Development of Antenna Measurement System Using Distributed Local Oscillators and Mixers
abstract: In this paper, we propose an antenna measurement system using distributed LOs(local oscillators) and mixers. The sensitivity and dynamic range of the antenna measurement system improved, because the proposed system minimizes the losses of RF and LO cables due to short cable lengths. As a result of measuring the insertion loss of antenna pairs using the proposed system, the sensitivity was improved by more than 20 dB compared to the conventional system.

articleTitle: Grid Searching Method in Polar Coordinate for PD Location in Substation
abstract: Grid searching method in rectangle coordinate is widely adopted for Partial Discharge (PD) location using Ultra High Frequency (UHF) sensor array in substation, which cannot fully take advantage of relative high angle locating precision of TDOA algorithm. This paper proposes a new grid searching method in polar coordinate and defines sector shape as searching grid. A sector grid with PD source is located by traversal, which is further divided into smaller sector for iteration until locating accuracy requirement is satisfied. Simulation shows the effectiveness of this method. Application example in a substation verifies the high reliability in angle location.

articleTitle: Low-Noise Measurement Setup for Single-Electron Pumps
abstract: Single-electron pumps (SEPs) applied as quantum current sources are a fundamental part of a future quantum triangle experiment. To characterize an SEP in a reasonably short time, a low-noise setup is needed. We present an improved measurement setup tailored for current measurements on SEP, characterized by a low-noise wiring and a new variant of the ultrastable low-noise current amplier (ULCA). The evaluation shows that the setup is suitable for measuring a 100 pA current with a relative uncertainty of 0.1 μA/A within about 14 hours.

articleTitle: Development of a Specialized Hydrostatic Comparator for the Accurate Density Determination of Natural Silicon Spheres: A Novel Method for a Primary Realization of the Unit Kilogram
abstract: A novel method to primary realize the soon-to-be redefined unit of mass, kilogram, is presented. The new approach will accurately relate the Planck constant to spheres manufactured from natural silicon. Therefore, the precisely known isotopical composition of a 28Si sphere will be transferred to a sphere made of natural silicon with a relative uncertainty of 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>. To achieve this objective, the concept of a newly developed hydrostatic comparator, which combines the Archimedes principle with a magnetic suspension coupling, is discussed. This combination allows to improve the major uncertainty contribution of this type of instrument - the temperature stability.

articleTitle: Radiation Pressure Measurement for Small Mass and Force Standard Using Voltage Balance Apparatus Developed at NMIJ
abstract: The radiation pressure force has been widely considered in a wide range of fields, such as microscopic optomechanics, plasmonics, astronautics, and metrology. The precision measurement of radiation pressure force, especially in a fashion traceable to the International System of Units (SI), is of importance. In this work, by using a new force balance system being developed at NMIJ, which can be calibrated by SI traceable standard, the radiation pressure force of optical laser was determined and compared to a load obtained by small mass standards.

articleTitle: A High Precision Multi-Ratio Three-Stage Current Transformer (CT) for Loss Measurements of Extra High Voltage (EHV) Three-Phase Shunt Reactors with Test Voltages up to 1100 kV
abstract: An overview of the development and performance of special high precision multi-ratio three-stage CT and its application for loss measurement of EHV three-phase shunt reactors With AC test voltages up to 1100 kV at Royal SMIT Transformers are presented and discuss. It features current ratios of 500A/1A, 400A/1A, 300A/1A, 200A/1A, and 100A/1A with ratio errors within 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in both magnitude and phase with burdens up to 1.0 Ω and at power frequencies of 50 Hz - 60 Hz.

articleTitle: Calibration of AC Shunts at Frequencies Up to 10 kHz Using Digital Sampling
abstract: This paper describes a calibration system for AC shunts using digital sampling. It provides both ratio errors and phase displacements of a shunt under test with respect to a reference shunt. In its basic configuration, the calibration system operates at currents of up to 10 A and frequencies of up to 10kHz. The expanded uncertainties (k=2) of the described calibration system are estimated to be better than 30 μA/A for magnitude and 30 μrad for phase at 10 kHz, and lower than these at lower frequencies.

articleTitle: Faraday Balance for Measuring Temperature Coefficient of Magnetic Moment of Permanent Magnet
abstract: A new Faraday balance for measuring temperature coefficient (TC) of magnetic moment of permanent magnet has been designed and evaluated. The gradient field is generated by a cylindrical electromagnet. The direction of the magnetic moment of the sample and the gradient field is in same vertical axis. As temperature interval is 10 K, the standard uncertainty of TC using this method is 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: AC Magnetometer Calibrations from 50 Hz up to 100 kHz at NMIJ
abstract: National metrology institute of Japan developed a system for calibrations of AC magnetometers at 50 Hz-60 Hz in 2012. However, demands for calibrations of AC magnetometers in high frequencies are increasing specially in the field of EMC measurement. In this paper, the AC magnetic field standard system is reevaluated and applied to AC magnetometer calibrations in high frequencies. The highest frequency is up to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Sampling Measurement of a 20-V RMS Sine Wave Using an Inductive Voltage Divider and an AC-Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: We have performed a differential sampling measurement of a sine wave with voltages up to the root-mean squared (RMS) amplitude of 20 V by combining an inductive voltage divider and an 10 V AC-programmable Josephson voltage standard. Expanding the voltage range of this technique enables the calibration of a calibrator and a digital voltmeter above the RMS amplitude of 10 V. The operating principle and a preliminary result are presented. The Type-A uncertainty of 0.2 μV/V is achieved with the technique when measuring a sine wave from the calibrator with RMS amplitude of 20 V at the frequency of 62.5 Hz.

articleTitle: Status of the Vacuum Birefringence Search at BMV
abstract: We present the current status and outlook of the Biréfringence Mangetique du Vide (BMV) project. The BMV experiment is a polarimetric search for the QED predicted anisotropy of vacuum in the presence of external electromagnetic fields. The main challenge faced in this fundamental test is the measurement of polarization ellipticity on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup>.

articleTitle: DC Comparison of a Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard and a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: We present the first dc comparison of a programmable Josephson voltage standards and a pulse-driven Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) at 3 V. Both circuits are mounted side-by-side on the cold stage of a cryocooler. The relative agreement achieved was better than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. This measurement allowed us to identify systematic errors of the JAWS system. An undesired current injection from the JAWS isolation amplifier into the measurement circuit was responsible for an error voltage of a few nanovolts.

articleTitle: Influence of Reflection Area on Calibration Accuracy by Single Antenna Method Using Broadband Antenna
abstract: We have already proposed the single antenna method for an antenna gain measurement of the log-periodic dipole array antenna (LPDA) and the double ridged guide horn antenna (DRGH). Our proposed single antenna method uses the metal ground plane as the electric mirror. In the measurement, the DRGH is set perpendicularly to the ground plane and electromagnetic absorbing materials are covered the ground plane for changing the reflection area of the ground plane. In the case of 3 m diameter of the reflection area at the antenna height of 5 m above the ground plane, the proposed method can completely separate the direct wave from other undesired waves from the absorbing materials. Further, we show the estimated antenna gain using Friis transmission formula at the phase center distance for our single antenna method.

Author Keywords: Reflection area of metal ground plane

articleTitle: Thermal Transfer Standard Calibrations Using a Pulse-Driven AC Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: We calibrate a commercial thermal transfer standard Fluke 792A with a pulse-driven ac Josephson voltage standard containing 6400 junctions. The ac-dc difference of the thermal transfer standard is presented for frequencies ranging from 2 kHz to 100 kHz with 10 mV applied to the 22 mV range and 100 mV applied to the 220 mV range. Calibration uncertainties are also estimated in detail.

articleTitle: Frequency Dependence Evaluation of CENAM Calculable Resistors
abstract: This paper presents the evaluation results of 1 kΩ and 10 kΩ CENAM calculable resistors using as reference a 1 kΩ METAS calculable resistor, by means of 1:1 and 10:1 ratios measurements, respectively. The measurements show an agreement better than \pmb0.35 μΩ/Ω through the audio-frequency range for the \pmb10 kΩ CENAM resistor. An analysis of the possible reasons of the observed linear frequency dependence in the 1 kΩ CENAM calculable resistors is also presented.

articleTitle: Dynamic Measurement for DC Electrical Energy
abstract: With more and more power consumption, DC electrical energy measurement is coming into an urgent need. And a new DC electrical energy measurement instrument is developed, which can measure power and energy for both static and dynamic signal. High-speed sampling method is adopted to get all the original information of the input signal and then obtain the time domain information by real-time hardware operation (FPGA). As a result of this, as long as the rate of data acquisition is high enough, the original information will quickly approach the actual measured signal.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Reference DC Current Transducer with AC Distortion for Railway Applications
abstract: To assess the reliability of DC energy measurement equipment on board trains, a setup was developed to calibrate current transducers at DC currents up to 900 A with major AC distortion. The reference transducer used is a high-precision zeroflux current transformer, which is calibrated under non-distorted conditions with 1 μV/V uncertainty (k = 2). The influence of AC distortion on the DC output of this reference transducer was found to be within a few parts in 106. Since the accuracy of the total energy measurement function of railway traction units needs to be on the order of 0.1 %, this is an excellent result.

articleTitle: Ultracold Atom Gravimeter
abstract: Atom interferometry allows for the realisation of inertial sensors based on laser cooled atoms. Their limits in performances, both in terms of accuracy and stability, are linked to the temperature of the atomic cloud, in the low μK range, and more specifically, to the residual ballistic expansion of the atomic sources in the laser beams. To overcome these limits, we use as a source ultracold atoms in the nano-kelvin range in our absolute atom gravimeter.

articleTitle: A New Period Measurement Method Based on Phase-sensitive Detection for Beam Balance Oscillator
abstract: The oscillation period of a beam balance oscillator is influenced by the ground vibrations via the displacements of the central pivot. In this paper, an analytical solution for the kinetic equation of the balance beam is deduced when periodic horizontal vibrations are considered. A new method based on phase-sensitive detection technique is proposed to improve the accuracy of oscillation period determination. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach has a much better anti-disturbance capability than the general one.

articleTitle: Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters with Increased Sensitivity Operated in Hermetically Sealed Housings Filled with Noble Gas
abstract: The sensitivity of planar multijunction thermal converters (PMJTCs) was significantly increased by filling the housing with noble gases, preferably xenon or krypton. The performance was observed for more than one year and no degradation of sensitivity was found. Also the frequency response of the AC-DC transfer difference remains unchanged at high frequencies and even improves below 40 Hz. Using the lowest at present manufacturable heater resistance of 90 Ω with the noble gas filling, AC-DC transfer down to less than 70 mV compared to about 100 mV in air becomes possible.

articleTitle: Precision Active Arm Bridge with Two Channel Voltage Source for Resistance Measurements of the Standards
abstract: Precision active arm bridge with two channel voltage source is being developed to improve high resistance measurements and scaling from 100 MΩ to 100 TΩ. Preliminary tests of the bridge have been made. The tests confirmed accuracy and stability of a new two-channel voltage source designed to be used in the bridge.

articleTitle: Development of Thin-Film Resistors Fabricated on an A1N Substrate for High-Voltage AC-DC Transfer Standards
abstract: The voltage dependence of ac-dc transfer differences occurs during step-up processes of over 300 V. The occurrence of voltage dependence may be partly due to Joule heating, which leads to changes in the resistance of the resistor and temperature dependence of the dielectric losses on the resistor coating. To reduce the voltage dependence of ac-dc transfer differences, thin-film range resistors with values ranging from 32 to 300 kΩ have been developed. For these thin-film range resistors, negligible voltage dependence has been observed at the voltage range from 100 to 1000 V.

articleTitle: Establishment of Reference Power Standard at SASO NMCC and GULFMET Bilateral Comparison
abstract: A well-known 3458A based digital sampling wattmeter was established for power and harmonics measurements at SASO NMCC. Its compact design and synchronized to the power source makes the standard unique for the calibrations needed by nationwide laboratories and industry. 40 ppm and 200 ppm are the first estimations in measurement uncertainties for power and harmonics, respectively. And, the first power comparison was organized under GULFMET.EM-S2 in order to evaluate the performance of the standard.

articleTitle: Errors of Multiplying D/A Converters Used for Precise AC Voltage Division
abstract: High-resolution multiplying digital-to-analog converters (MDACs) are often used as digitally controlled AC voltage dividers in precise instruments and measurement systems. Proper application of these converters requires knowledge of their parameters, especially amplitude and phase errors, which are usually not specified by MDAC manufacturers. The paper presents phase errors of selected commercial 16- and I8-bit MDACs measured with a dedicated sampling system. These errors were determined as a function of frequency of the divided sinusoidal voltage and as a function of the MDAC digital input word.

articleTitle: Calibration of the Absolute Linearity of Lock-in Amplifiers
abstract: This paper describes the development of a system capable to calibrate the linearity of lock-in amplifiers in their 1 μV range for frequencies between 20 Hz and 1 kHz. This system is based on cascaded inductive voltage dividers (IVD). These dividers have been especially designed to maximize their input impedance and to have minimal influence on the previous stage. The cascaded topology of this system reduces the uncertainty for very large ratios (> 1000:1) and reaches measurement uncertainties below 1 nV at 10 μV.

articleTitle: The Status of PTB's Nanonewton Force Facility
abstract: The nanonewton force facility of PTB (Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, Germany), first presented in [1]-[3], has been significantly improved. In this work, we will demonstrate that the facility is able to measure forces in the range below 1 μN with a resolution below 5 pN and an uncertainty below 2.7 % for a measured force of 1 nN at a measuring duration of about 20 s. We will demonstrate the use of the facility as a calibration device. We will also present measurements methods and the results for the spring constant of a cantilever, the contact potential difference and the negative light pressure.

articleTitle: Superconducting Single-Electron Transistor as a 3e-Cotunneling Turnstile
abstract: In a superconducting single-electron transistor (SSET), we demonstrate a charge turnstile regime based on higher-order tunneling as a major transport mechanism. In this regime, the quantized current appears as a sequence of Cooper pair-electron cotunneling events cycled by a periodic gate signal and transferring a discrete three-electron charge per cycle. Operating as a relatively slow, higher-order tunneling system, the 3e-turnstile exhibits stable current plateaus in the sub-pA range. The device could be useful for generating precise ultralow currents as well as for experimental evaluation of cotunneling error rates in electron turnstiles.

articleTitle: Optical Simulation of the Influence of Spheres with Local Deviations on the Radius Value
abstract: The wavefront reflected by a real sphere was supposed to influence significantly the value of the volume determination. Therefore, optical simulations were performed to investigate the wavefront aberration and the results of simulated and inputted topographies are compared. To evaluate the valid boundary of the raytracing software a synthetic sphere with one local deviation from roundness was simulated. The software was validated with a precision of 0.01 nm for a standard sphere of 50 nm form deviation. In succession the contribution of the wavefront reflection in the uncertainty budget could be reduced for various spheres.

articleTitle: Current Comparator Based Current Divider
abstract: The paper describes a current divider (or splitter), i.e., a device that allows the splitting of an alternating current (ac) in two parts in a precise and accurate current ratio. It is based on current comparator techniques so that precise current ratios can be attained with ratio errors bearing parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>. A binary current divider can be made virtually exact (i.e., with unitary current ratio errors of the order of some 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> only), if aided by electronic flux error compensation. Further, coupled transmission lines modeling can assess its current ratio errors over frequency. A current divider finds application in many areas of ac metrology as in highly accurate impedance bridges and current measurements.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Evaluation of Differential Sampling System Using AC Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: In this paper, we analyzed the error transfer function of AC voltage differential sampling system which is based on switching measurement. Then, three factors, the relative phase, the number of steps and the sampling window, that influence the uncertainty of the RMS amplitude measurement are identified. After evaluation of those three components, we concluded that the combined standard uncertainty budget is 0.3 μ V/V.

articleTitle: An Improved Mobile Calibration Standard for Transformer Loss Measurement Systems
abstract: Existing mobile calibration standard used for onsite calibration of transformer loss measurement systems has been upgraded. Master-slave configuration of programmable power sources is replaced with the external triggering and synchronization method which ensures the system stability below 50 ppm. Resolution in phase-settings between voltage and current generation is now improved about 2-digits down to 1 m°. And, measurement results are automatically evaluated with the corrected calibration values of system components.

articleTitle: Extensive Measurements to Define Boundary Conditions for Efficient AC and DC Residential Houses
abstract: This paper compares the wiring systems at four voltage levels (12V DC, 24V DC, 48V DC and 230V AC) to feed the DC appliances through a regulated DC source. Possible wiring cases in an existing residential house are based on the power rating of load, conductor length and its area. Few cases have been experimentally tested in previous research work, but extensive experimentation and measurement are required to confirm the boundary conditions for the wiring systems. In this paper, validated models based on actual measurements of 184 experimental cases were used to define the boundary conditions that could help residential consumers to select the suitable wiring system for 62400 possible cases.

articleTitle: Portable DC Voltage and Resistance Reference with Switching Unit for Calibration of Electrical Precision Multifunction Instruments
abstract: A portable temperature controlled DC Voltage and DC Resistance Reference with Switching Unit (RSU) has been developed at National Institute of Metrological Research (INRIM) to calibrate multifunction electrical instruments involving 10 V, a 1 Ω and a 10 kΩ Standards. The resistors are made with two resistors nets while the 10 V is a low noise-drift INRIM-projected circuit. Preliminary measurement over one-month period shows standards uncertainties span from 3.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> to 6.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>, suitable for artifact calibration. With a real clock calendar, the RSU can show both the RSU Standards calibration values and updated ones between two calibrations according to an internal algorithm.

articleTitle: A Bias Method for an AC Josephson Quantum Voltage Standard
abstract: We describe an AC bias technique for a SNS Josephson junction array. The method is based on array voltage sources and a bias circuit has been designed to provide the bias current through the series resistance of the voltage source. The experiments for bias circuit characteristics have been carried out, which demonstrate the circuit offers a satisfactory dynamic characteristic and stability.

articleTitle: 10 TΩ and 100 TΩ Resistance Comparison Between NIST and AIST
abstract: We report the results of a comparison of 10 TΩ and 100 TΩ high resistance standards between the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the National Institute for Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST). Three standard resistors were hand carried between both laboratories, a 100 TΩ from NIST and a 10 TΩ and 100 TΩ from AIST. The two laboratories agreed to within 100 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at 10 TΩ and 500 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at 100 TΩ. The comparison results have given both laboratories an external check of their measurement systems and scaling processes to 100 TΩ.

articleTitle: Uncertainty of Phasor Measurement Unit Calculated by Means of Monte Carlo Method
abstract: Whole measurement chain of a Phasor Measurement Unit was simulated and uncertainty of Total Vector Error (TVE) has been calculated using Monte Carlo Method. The results showed the most important uncertainty contributions and behaviour of the probability distribution function of the output uncertainty. Asymmetrical uncertainties of TVE have to be calculated to obtain proper values.

articleTitle: Validity Evaluation of Application of TRL Calibration Method to Dielectric Waveguide Measurement by Electromagnetic Simulation
abstract: We have proposed to apply the Thru-Reflect-Line (TRL) calibration to the evaluation of dielectric waveguides to improve the measurement accuracy. When evaluating a dielectric waveguide, it is necessary to convert it into metallic transmission lines to connect to measurement ports of a vector network analyzer. Mismatches in connections of different types of cables lead to errors in measurements. We solved this problem by using the TRL calibration kits made of the same low-loss dielectric material as the dielectric waveguide under test. By electromagnetic simulations, we demonstrated the usefulness of the proposed technique at 28 GHz band.

articleTitle: Harmonics Effects on Microwave Low-Power Measurement
