The target combined standard uncertainty for the calibration of the 100 Ω/(R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>/2) ratio (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> is the von Klitzing constant) is a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of the Influence of Electrostatic Charge on High Resistance Guarded Hamon Transfer Devices Accuracy
abstract: Electrostatic charge can influence the accuracy of Hamon transfer resistance ratio. In the paper the results of simulations on influence of electrostatic charge on accuracy of high resistance guarded Hamon transfer devices resistance ratio are presented.

articleTitle: High Voltage Metrology with Collinear Laser Spectroscopy
abstract: We present results of laser spectroscopic high voltage measurements on the 5 ppm relative uncertainty level using a pump and probe scheme on Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions. With the two-stage laser interaction and with a reference measurement we can eliminate systematic effects like differences in contact potentials of electrode materials, thermo-electric voltages, and the unknown starting potential of the ions in the ion source. Our measurements are compatible with the 5 ppm precision limits of the high voltage dividers used for comparison and demonstrate an unprecedented increase in the accuracy of laser-based high voltage measurements by a factor of 20.

articleTitle: NIST Kibble Balance Performance
abstract: The fourth generation Kibble balance at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has been operational and used to measure the value of the Planck constant from Fall 2015 to Spring 2017. Since then, researchers have been working on upgrades and checking the robustness of the experiment in preparation for the redefinition of the SI.

articleTitle: SIM Key Comparison of S-Parameters SIM.EM.RF-K5b.CL
abstract: The first RF key comparison within the Inter-American Metrology System (SIM) Regional Metrology Organization has been carried out. The purpose of it was to establish the degree of equivalence of scattering parameters measurements of both 1-port and 2-port coaxial devices among national metrology institutes (NMIs) that belong to SIM region and in support of CIPM Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA). The travelling standards were four devices with Type-N coaxial connectors and 50 Ω of characteristic impedance: a matched load, a mismatched load and two attenuators of 3 dB and 20 dB. Four SIM institutes participated in the comparison as well as NPLI.

articleTitle: A Laser-Pumped Cs−4He Magnetometer for Metrology
abstract: This paper describes a laser-pumped cesium-helium magnetometer (CHM) with high polarization efficiency. The magnetic-resonance signal amplitude has been improved by one order of magnitude comparing with the lamp-pumped scheme. The optimal parameters for increasing the signal-to-noise ratio of the magnetometer are obtained and discussed.

articleTitle: Parallelized Single Electron Pumps Based on Gate-Tunable Quantum Dot
abstract: In order to increase the output current level, we have fabricated a parallelized pump with two gate-tunable quantum-dot pumps based on GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure. Each pump device is composed of multiple gates forming a quantum dot whose potential shapes and barrier heights are tunable. At optimally potential-tuned condition, we have confirmed that the parallelized pump could be considered as a single pump and its theoretically estimated accuracy stays almost the same as the single one within the theoretical resolution. Thus we produce I=192 pA at 0.6 GHz with an expected accuracy as low as 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> level.

articleTitle: Pressure Sensitivity Coefficients of the BIPM Secondary Voltage Standards
abstract: At the 2016 CPEM, we presented the results of the re-evaluation of the temperature sensitivity coefficients of the BIPM secondary DC voltage standards based on Zener diodes. These standards are used as travelling references within the Key Comparison identified as BIPM.EM-K11 in the CIPM-MRA framework. As a follow-up of this work, we present here the reevaluation of the pressure sensitivity coefficients of the same standards. Since the standards are now fully characterized, their 10 V output was calibrated, for several consecutive days, using three completely independent measurement setups, based on three different Josephson Voltage Standards (JVSs). The results show that a repeatable significant systematic error of up to 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> can appear for some specific artifacts depending on the operated measurement setup. We suspect the intrinsic properties (output impedance and leakage resistance to ground) of these standards to be responsible for the observed discrepancy.

Author Keywords: calibration of Zener-based secondary voltage standards

articleTitle: Cryogenic Primary Standard for Optical Fiber Power Measurement
abstract: NIST has completed commissioning a new, state-of-the-art cryogenic primary standard for optical fiber power measurement and calibration. It establishes for the first time, a direct traceability route between the device under test and primary standard. A silicon micro-machined planar detector, incorporating a carbon nanotube absorber and superconducting transition edge temperature sensor, forms the basis of the radiometer, whilst advanced thermal filtering ensures noise-free operation. Measurement repeatability below 50ppm is routinely achieved. The measurement uncertainty (k=\pmb2) is 0.40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, a 20% improvement on NIST's previous capability. The new primary standard benefits the telecommunications industry.

articleTitle: Thermal Gradients in the Si Lattice Parameter Measurement
abstract: We report about numerical and experimental investigations of the thermal gradients in the INRIM's combined X-ray and optical interferometer used to measure the lattice parameter of silicon.

articleTitle: Infrared & Visible Ultrastable Optical Frequency Standard
abstract: We report on the development of a three-wavelength optical frequency standard (OFS: ω, 2ω, 3ω), frequency stabilized to a narrow iodine hyperfine line around 514 nm. To bridge the frequency gap between the infrared and the green ranges of the optical domain (1542 nm → 514 nm), we use an efficient third harmonic generation process, based on two cascaded Lithium Niobate crystals, arranged in an original optical configuration. Up to 300 mW of green power is obtained from 800 mW of IR power, corresponding to an unprecedented demonstration of an optical conversion efficiency η = P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3ω</sub>/P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</sub> ~ 36 % in continuous wave regime. Iodine Doppler-free spectroscopy technique is used to frequency stabilize this OFS against a narrow hyperfine line at 514 nm yielding to a frequency stability σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>(τ)=2.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-14</sup> τ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1/2</sup>, with a minimum value of 7.3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> after 200 s of integration time.

articleTitle: Calibration of CISPR Detectors
abstract: This paper describes calibration methods for calibration of CISPR detectors in accordance with standard CISPR 16-1-1. SIQ has developed a calibration system based on burst modulation and pulsed RF technique, which provide results comparable with pulse generator method described in the standard. Both methods have also been compared.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Calibrating Automatic Direct Current Comparator Resistance Bridges
abstract: In order to reduce measurement uncertainty of the resistance \pmb(10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> Ω ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>Ω) due to the uncertainty component from the automatic direct current comparator resistance bridge (ADCCRB) ratio error, a novel method based on a direct current comparator (DCC) and two same nominal resistances is presented. The measurement uncertainty of the ADCCRB ratio error is largely dependent on DCC and Type A uncertainty of the ADCCRB. It is shown by the experimental results that the measurement uncertainty from the ADCCRB (ratio: 10:1) is less than \pmb3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>, k=2.

articleTitle: Usage of Silicon Crystals to Determine the Avogadro and Planck Constants
abstract: Crystals produced from silicon that is highly enriched in the<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si isotope were used to determine the Avogadro constant by means of the X-ray crystal density (XRCD) method. The results were included in the special CODATA adjustment for fixing the values of the Avogadro and Planck constants in the revised International System of Units (SI), which is scheduled to come into force on World Metrology Day, 2019. In this work, the XRCD method is outlined, results are discussed and future developments anticipated.

articleTitle: Pyrolytic Carbon: Applications of Diamagnetic Levitation in Metrology
abstract: This paper presents some current or potential applications in metrology implementing the diamagnetic property of pyrolytic carbon (PyC). The magnetic repulsion force acting between a piece of PyC placed in a magnetic flux density can be used as magnetic spring either to control the position of the sensitive sensor part or to detect change of a physical quantity to be measured. Several examples of PyC-based sensors are presented.

articleTitle: Traceable Analog Detector for Quantum Radiometry
abstract: This paper presents an analog detector that is directly traceable to the traditional optical radiometry primary standard at the level of 100 μW and performs as the transfer standard detector for measurements of photon flux levels of about one hundred thousand photon/s with an uncertainty below 2%. The detector has been successfully applied in arrange of measurements that used to be considered exclusively accessible to quantum photon counting detectors.

articleTitle: Investigation of Applicability of Heat Exchange Gas for Cooling of Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard Chip
abstract: Thermal management of programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) chips is important for their stable operation. The applicability of a heat exchange gas to thermal management has been investigated. The finite element analysis showed that the temperature reduction of the PJVS chip due to the gas conduction was approximately 1 %.

articleTitle: Minimize Temperature Effect in High Precision Optical Fiber Based Range Measurement Calibration System
abstract: A high precision calibration range measurement system based on optical fiber switches and fiber coils network is described in this paper. To reach the high measurement precision, the phase stabilized optical fiber (PSOF), is used as delay coil to minimize the temperature dependence of transmission delay time. The temperature error can be decreased by 11 times compare with using single-mode optical fiber.

articleTitle: H-Coil Measurement Method of High Performance Electrical Steel Sheet
abstract: This paper describes the current situation of electric steel iron loss measurement, the current measurement method (M.C) has been difficult to meet the development of high performance electrical steel. It has been verified that the H-coil method is more accurate and more advanced than M.C method.

articleTitle: Status of the Realization and Dissemination of the Kilogram via Silicon Spheres
abstract: Silicon spheres are qualified standards for the realization and dissemination of the kilogram according to the new approach of the revised SI. Moderate costs, robustness, and practice oriented use are unique features. The Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) is running two projects that will bring the advantages to high level end users. The international project “Si-Trust”, allows interested national metrology authorities to get familiar with the handling of 1kg Si-spheres. The project “Si-kg” is establishing a technological and commercial infrastructure. A first silicon sphere made of the isotope 28 was sold to an Asian institute in 2017.

articleTitle: A PMU Calibration System
abstract: There is a need for traceable calibrations of Phasor measurement units, which measures the phase angle of power system signals with respect to the universal time. This paper describes the design of such a calibration system. The system utilizes a fast A-D converter, synchronized to the Swedish time and frequency realization. The speed and synchronization makes the calibration and adjustment fast and relatively straight-forward. Coaxial dividers and shunts are used for system control. The goal is a three-phase system with an angular uncertainty in the order of, or better than ±0.002° or ±100 ns.

articleTitle: A Synchronized Current-Comparator-Based Power Bridge for Calibrating Analog Merging Units
abstract: A synchronized current-comparator-based power bridge for calibrating analog merging units at power frequencies of 60 Hz and 50 Hz is described. Analog merging units take analog signals from instrument transformers, convert them into digital form, pack the sampled values into Ethernet frames conforming to the IEC 61850-9-2 LE specification and stream the frames to other equipment in a digital substation for further processing. Since the sampled values are used for protection and metering, the merging units need to be calibrated. The expanded uncertainties (k=2) of the described calibration system are estimated to be better than 30 μA/A for magnitude and 60 μrad for phase.

articleTitle: Compensation of Complex Frequency Errors of Voltage Instrument Transformers
abstract: The paper focuses on a system for the compensation of the frequency response of voltage instrument transformers through the use of a digital filter. After a brief review of the compensation method, the performances of the digital filter in the correction of the frequency response of voltage transformers with first resonances within the 50th harmonic are investigated and quantified. Examples of implementation of the filter both in LabVIEW, for off-line correction, and by FPGA, enabling realtime correction, are given. First results show a reduction of the voltage transformer errors up to two orders of magnitude at the first resonance frequency.

articleTitle: A Sampling Wattmeter with Extended Frequency Range
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a sampling wattmeter for the measurement of sinusoidal active and reactive power over the 50 Hz to 6 kHz frequency range, 20 V to 600 V voltage range, and 0.05 A to 80 A current range. The wattmeter is capable of measuring sinusoidal and distorted voltage and current signals with up to 100 harmonics of the fundamental frequency component. Details of the system design, measurement techniques, and significant sources of error are presented.

articleTitle: Two-Step Mirror Model for the Optimization of the Magnetic Field Generated by Coils Inside Magnetic Shielding
abstract: A partly analytical method for calculating the magnetic field generated by coils in a closed magnetic shield is presented. The field distortion caused by the high-permeability boundary is analyzed by using the improved mirror method combined with a finite element method. This approach leads to an analytical solution which can be calculated much faster than a full FEM solution. By applying this model, we could calculate the optimal parameters for a four square-coil setup to produce the most homogenous magnetic field in the center of the Berlin magnetically shielded room (BMSR-2) with acceptable accuracy.

articleTitle: Calibration of the Second Generation of Ultrastable Low-Noise Current Amplifiers Using a Cryogenic Current Comparator
abstract: Following the established two-stage conception for the realization of the ultrastable low-noise current amplifier, new variants have been tailored to meet the special requirements of demanding applications. Changes include new components selected according to stability criteria and new design parameters. For most of these variants, calibration capabilities based on a cryogenic current comparator setup have been developed. The overview given in this contribution will focus on aspects of the achievable measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: Bridging the LF-RF gap for Calibration of the RLC Meters
abstract: This paper describes economic way of bridging the well known LF-RF gap in the impedance metrology for means of calibration of RLC autobalance bridges. A simple calculable resistance standard capable of operation up to at least 100 MHz was developed. It was compared to the RF chip resistors characterized by means of the s-matrix technique. Achieved expanded uncertainty (k=2) at 100 MHz was 1.4 % which is sufficient for calibration of impedance analyzers. Furthermore, the standard was realized in the two terminal construction so it can be used as a load correction for regular measurements.

articleTitle: Allan-Deviation Measurements of Gate-Tunable Single Electron Pumps with the Ultrastable Low-Noise Current Amplifier
abstract: We characterized KRISS precision measurement system by measuring the Allan deviation of the quantized current generated by GaAs/AIGaAs gate-tunable electron pumps, where the current was amplified by the ultrastable low-nose current amplifier (ULCA) developed by the PTB. The Allan deviation of a phosphor bronze wire generally used at cryogenic temperature showed a white noise level of about 18 fA Hz-1I2. The noise level of the electron pump was improved by a factor 4 with a specific choice of cryogenic cables.

articleTitle: Parasitic Displacements Measurement of Suspended Coil in Joule Balance NIM-2
abstract: This paper describes the measurement method of parasitic displacements arising from the misalignment of suspended coil. This method is based on the optical paths of interferometer system in joule balance. Except for optical elements for interference measurement, no extra elements are needed for parasitic displacements measurement in vacuum. All the parasitic displacements are calculated from the interference optical signals. This method can simplify the structure of suspended coil in joule balance, and also measures the parasitic displacements of suspended coil in reality.

articleTitle: Improved SMD-Based Capacitance Standards
abstract: We have developed improved SMD-based capacitance standards of a nominal value of 10 nF. Other values in a wide range are also possible. The standards feature a small relative deviation from nominal (less than 10×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>), a low dissipation factor (less than 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>), and a small temperature coefficient (0.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>/K) which strongly reduces the requirements for temperature control. Here, we report on the design and the assembly procedure.

articleTitle: AC Internal Resistance Measurement of Batteries
abstract: The AC internal resistance measurement method of batteries is introduced, which is based on synchronous sampling method by comparing with standard resistance. The improved DFT algorithm is used to eliminate influence of noise. A simulated resistor based on two-stage inductive voltage divider is designed to verify the method. The internal resistance of lithium ion batteries at 1 kHz are measured.

articleTitle: Crest Factor Minimization for Multitone Waveform Synthesis Using the Clipping Algorithm
abstract: Optimizing the harmonic phases of a multitone waveform to achieve a lower crest factor is beneficial to reduce the distortions generated by nonlinear electronic components and increase the signal to noise ratio in precision measurements. This paper uses two clipping algorithms to minimize the crest factor, which take less time for calculations compared to the nonlinear Chebyshev approximation algorithm. With the optimization, the crest factor is minimized to about 1.4 for both Schroeder and random multitone waveforms. Moreover, the maximum tone amplitude is increased significantly when using the ac Josephson voltage standard for waveform synthesis.

articleTitle: Towards a Quantum Standard for Absolute Pressure Measurements in the Range 200 Pa to 20 kPa Based on a Superconducting Microwave Cavity
abstract: We present a novel pressure standard for helium gas based on the measurement of resonance frequencies of a superconducting cavity and ab initio calculations of the thermophysical properties of helium. It should improve significantly the accuracy of measurements in the range 200 Pa to 20 kPa.

articleTitle: The Simulations of the Effect of the External Field in the Joule Balance
abstract: Due to the movement of the main magnet, the effect of the external field is a critical problem in the joule balance. The FEM simulations of the external field both in the electromagnet system and permanent magnet system are performed in this paper. The results show that although the error caused by the external field is much smaller in the permanent magnet system than that in the electromagnet system, it still needs to be further reduced. More efficient solutions should be considered to eliminate the effect of the external field when the permanent magnet system is used.

articleTitle: Low Resolution Stochastic Flash ADC for High Precision Energy and RMS Voltage Measurements for Smart Grid
abstract: This paper describes 4-bit Stochastic Flash ADC based instrument, with its low-resolution compensated by adding dither (uniform noise) to the input signal and calculation of the output average value over a finite time period, resulting in low part count, high sampling speed and low error. Precision of this instrument is user controlled - the longer the period of measurement, higher the measurement precision. This enables measurement of electrical quantities over long time intervals, such as electrical energy and RMS voltage in a power grid. For 60-second measurement period, precision is 58 ppm, and for 180 s it is 34 ppm.

articleTitle: Effect of Step Response Measurement Arrangement on the Correction of Lightning Impulses Measured with Ultra-High-Voltage Dividers
abstract: Ultra-high-voltage (UHV) lightning impulse voltage dividers normally have limited bandwidth, which deforms the waveform of the measured impulse. The step response of the dividers can be used to correct the measured waveforms by deconvolution, reducing the errors of the impulse parameters. The circuit arrangement for measuring step response, however, may influence the measured step response and the corrected impulse waveforms. In this paper, two circuit arrangements of step response measurement were used in investigating the effect of different step responses on the corrected impulses. The lightning impulses measured using two UHV dividers were corrected and the errors of the impulse parameters before and after correction were determined. The results show that accurate correction can be made for the dividers without being affected by the external connection arrangement of the step response measurement.

articleTitle: WR-42 Waveguide Microcalorimeter for Thermistor Mount Calibration
abstract: This paper reports recent development progress of a new WR-42 (18 to 26.5 GHz) microcalorimeter in China. The waveguide microcalorimeter is designed for calibrating a thermistor mount (a common transfer power standard) in this frequency band. In the paper, development and measurement principle of the WR-42 microcalorimeter will be discussed. Performance evaluation of the microcalorimeter is carried out using a commercial thermistor mount (HP K486A, No. 1606) with uncertainty analysis.

articleTitle: Multifilar Resistors from DC up to 30 MHz
abstract: The function of the frequency dependence of resistance for bifilar resistor remains unchanged in the frequency range from DC to 30 MHz. The parameters of this function measured at one frequency make it possible to calculate the resistance at any other frequency of the range. These parameters are determined by the residual parameters of the resistor - its inductance and capacitance. Reducing the physical dimensions of the resistor leads to a decrease in its residual parameters and reduces of its frequency dependence.

articleTitle: Measurement of Grid Impedance at Harmonic Frequencies
abstract: The importance of impedance measurements in electricity grids at harmonic frequencies is discussed along with the measurement challenges. The potential use of infrequent disturbance events such as transients for harmonic signals to excite the measurement circuit is discussed. A method based on two phasor measurement units is then presented along with preliminary laboratory results.

articleTitle: Shimming and Performance of the Permanent Magnet for NIM-2
abstract: By May 2017, the uncertainty of NIM-2 joule balance is 2.4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>. The main uncertainty contribution is from the external field. To decrease it, a new permanent magnet and magnetic shielding are going to be used. Here, the construction and shimming of the permanent magnet are presented. A novel shape of the inner and outer yoke is designed to increase the consistency of the magnetic field when the magnet is repeatedly opened and closed. With two different shimming methods, the uniformity of the magnetic field is improved from 7.9 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> to below 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>.

articleTitle: A Quantum Hall Effect Kelvin Bridge for Resistance Calibration
abstract: We describe a resistance ratio bridge suitable for calibrating a four-terminal resistor of value close to the quantum Hall resistance. The bridge includes three quantum Hall elements, wired with multiple connections. The unique properties of the quantum Hall effect provide a Kelvin-like combining network and the rejection of wiring stray resistances. The bridge has a simple schematic and does not include any adjustable element: its reading is the deviation from equilibrium, measured as a small voltage ratio. Circuit network analysis predicts that a basic implementation of the bridge can reach a calibration accuracy in the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> range.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Zener Standard Drifts
abstract: This article presents the results of a study of Zener standards stability over a period one year. To estimate parameters of a linear drift, a weighted least squares fit is applied to calculate the parameters of the linear drift of the voltage output of the Zeners standards. These parameters were determined for different models of noise (white noise, flicker noise and a combination of the two noises). The influence of the volume of experimental data and that of the unevenness of their location within the estimation interval of the drift prediction and corresponding uncertainty were investigated.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performances of an Operational Absolute Quantum Gravimeter
abstract: The Absolute Quantum Gravimeter (AQG) is an industry-grade gravimeter measuring g with laser-cooled atoms, that has been developed by Muquans in close collaboration with RESIF (the French Seismologic and Geodetic Network, [2]) and the LNE-SYRTE laboratory. This paper reports on the evaluation of the first unit of the AQG and in particular on a statistical uncertainty on the measurement of g better than 1.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> m/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> that has been reached in various types of environment and for month-long continuous measurements. The relevance of the AQG for a use in metrological laboratories is also discussed.

articleTitle: Driving a Josephson Junction Array with a Mode-Locked Laser and a Photodiode
abstract: This paper describes development of a new technique to drive Josephson junction arrays (JJA). We have designed and built an optical pulse generator (up to 12 GHz pulse rate) based on a mode-locked laser to feed an ultra-fast photodiode which again can drive current pulses to a JJA. Our preliminary experiments show that precise direct current (dc) voltages can be realized with a JJA with 5000 junctions. The work ultimately aims at development of an arbitrary pulse pattern generator allowing generation of precise arbitrary voltage waveforms.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction Measurement in Electrical Steel and Amorphous Strip
abstract: Magnetostriction measurement of electrical steel and amorphous strip is becoming increasing important. Intensive work on establishing an IEC standard has been reviewed. Other 7 labs and NIM recently joined international comparison of magnetostriction in IEC. A magntetostriction measuring system with small uncertainty has been developed and calibrated in NIM. Typical results of magnetostriction on electrical steel and amorphous strip are presented.

articleTitle: Josephson Based Spectrum Analyzer
abstract: Differential measurements relative to a Josephson waveform provide very accurate measurements of ac waveforms. Pulse driven arrays, used in Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizers, can generate sine waves with very high spectral purity. These two Josephson based measurement tools can be combined to study undesired distortion components present in the frequency spectrum of high quality waveform generators. For a proof of principle experiment, we cancelled the fundamental tone of a waveform and measured the third harmonic that was generated.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a High-Order Sigma-Delta Continuous-Time Modulator
abstract: This paper describes the design and simulation of a high order sigma-delta loop filter to use in a feedback loop for the QuADC project. The project target specifications required the selection of a fourth order feedback loop to achieve them. The design includes two loop rates (100 MHz and 20 MHz), and the selected loop was a cascade of integrators with feedforward topology. The simulation results show that the target specification can be achieved by configuring the oversampling ratio and the digital filter according to the measurement bandwidth.

articleTitle: Characterization of PXI-Based Generators for Impedance Measurement Setups
abstract: This paper describes the comparison of properties of three commercially available multiphase digital ac voltage sources made as PXI modules. The research concerned their two-phase configuration for use in impedance bridges. Considering the assumed field of application, the most important parameters like the stability of amplitude ratio and phase difference as well as the total harmonic distortion and the spurious-free dynamic range was examined.

articleTitle: Calibration of AMN/LISN at SCL
abstract: The Standards and Calibration Laboratory (SCL) has developed a method to calibrate a single phasf <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pmb{50\ \Omega/50\ \mu \text{H}+} 5\ \Omega$</tex> V-network type Artificial Mains Network (AMN)/Line Impedance Stabilization Network (LISN) in accordance with the International Standard CISPR 16-1-2 over the frequency range 9 kHz to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: Medium Power Application of a Four-Port Reflectometer
abstract: This paper describes an application of a four-port reflectometer system to measure the reflection coefficient of a terminal load from 1 GHz to 2.5 GHz at about 150 W power level. The scattering parameters of the four-port reflectometer measured at low power have been experimentally proved to be applicable at medium power. The measurement results of the four-port reflectometer are presented and analyzed. This measurement method can be used at higher power level.

articleTitle: Microwave Method for Closure of Quasi-Spherical Resonator
abstract: Quasi-spherical microwave cavity resonators are widely used in primary thermometry. To realize high-accuracy microwave resonant frequency measurement, it is essential to close the two quasi-hemispheres correctly. We show how to do this using microwave resonance signals to monitor shape and sealing as torques to equatorial bolts are increased. The present resonator was closed with torques up to 105 cNm. The method should be useful to monitor the closing of other quasi-spherical cavities.

articleTitle: Four Terminal Pair Digital Sampling Impedance Bridge up to 1 MHz
abstract: This paper describes a new four terminal pair digital sampling impedance bridge for frequency range up to 1 MHz. The bridge was primarily designed for a calibration of a phase angle of the current shunts. However, the bridge is capable of comparing any impedance standards up to approximately 100 kΩ in a full complex plane. The experimental measurements of the known standards showed the bridge deviations is below 50 flO/O and below 500 urad at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Accuracy of Temperature Measurements of the Avogadro-Project
abstract: For the determination of the Avogadro constant via the XRCD-method the ratio of two temperature-dependent quantities, the unit cell volume and the sphere volume, need to be measured with the smallest possible uncertainties. Since both quantities show the same temperature dependency, only the reproducibility of the temperature measurements has to be taken into account. This paper summarizes the test measurements made for determining the accuracy of the temperature measurements of the standard platinum resistance thermometers which are used in the measurements of the silicon-lattice parameter at the INRIM and PTB, and the volume, at the NMIJ and PTB.

articleTitle: ANIST Testbed for Examining the Accuracy of Smart Meters Under High Harmonic Waveform Loads
abstract: Household and industrial electrical energy measurements are advancing into a Smart Grid stage, using solid-state watt-hour meters, called smart meters. As electrical products are also becoming more based on solid-state designs, such as LED lighting and dimmers, electrical loads are not purely resistive, but contain voltage and current spikes. This paper describes a testbed laboratory that will attempt to model LED household lighting loads, and correlate the energy measurements for changes in accuracy by various kinds of smart meters under unusual loads.

articleTitle: Effect of Coaxial Cables on Measurements Performed with Resistive Lightning Impulse Voltage Dividers
abstract: The effect of the coaxial cable type and length on the lightning impulse parameters is often neglected. However, studies have shown that the coaxial cable length can affect the parameters that are calculated according to IEC 60060-1:2010. This study investigates how different coaxial cables influence the impulse waveforms by measuring the input and output of the cable under test with a 2-channel digitizer. Non-standard lightning impulses were generated using an impulse voltage calibrator. Results indicate that coaxial cables attenuate the test voltage and increase both the front time and time-to-half value.

articleTitle: An Optoelectronic Pulse Drive for Quantum Voltage Synthesizer
abstract: An optoelectronic pulse drive system based on commercially available telecoms optoelectronic components and a field programmable gate array (FPGA) has been developed. The system was used to drive a Josephson junction array (JJA) to synthesize quantum-accurate voltage waveforms. Results from preliminary demonstration of the system are presented showing the synthesis of a 3.1 kHz sine wave.

articleTitle: Interleaved Matter-Wave Gyroscope with 3 × 10−10 rad.s−1 Stability
abstract: We present a matter-wave gyroscope with 11 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Sagnac area operating without dead times and at a sampling frequency of 3.75 Hz. This is achieved by interleaving the atom laser-cooling step and the interrogation of the atoms. We demonstrate a record short term sensitivity of 30 nrad.s-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. Hz-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which allows us to characterize and stabilize systematic effects below 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>rad.s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> after 15 000 seconds of integration time. Such level of stability competes with best long term stabilities obtained with fiber-optics gyroscopes, and paves the way for applications of cold-atom sensors in inertial navigation or geoscience.

articleTitle: A Simultaneously Comparison of Three Current Transformer Calibration Systems
abstract: This paper shows a novel method for simultaneous comparison of three current transformer calibration systems at power frequency. All three systems are designed for the calibration of high accuracy current transformers. The measuring method is also suitable for interlaboratory comparisons of calibration systems/methods. The paper gives a description of the novel measuring method and the compared measuring systems. The comparison results are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Evaluation for the INRIM Microcalorimeter
abstract: In recent years, several improvements have been made on the INRIM coaxial microcalorimeter with the aim to make more stable its operation and reduce the measurement uncertainty. Improvements concern the thermostat structure, the coaxial insulating lines, measurement software and electronics. A comprehensive uncertainty budget is here presented, that takes into account the main influence variables in the realization of the Radiofrequency and Microwaves (RF&MW) power standard at INRIM by means of the microcalorimetric technique. Details are also given on how some component has been determined.

articleTitle: Progress on the New NMIA Calculable Cross-Capacitor
abstract: A new calculable cross-capacitor and associated impedance measurement chain is being built at the National Measurement Institute Australia (NMIA). The new system is intended to reduce the uncertainty of the farad as realised by a calculable capacitor to a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>, an order of magnitude improvement on existing calculable capacitor systems. We report here on recent progress on the assembly of the calculable capacitor, specifically the measurement of the frequency dependent correction, and the final alignment of the electrodes.

articleTitle: Using of High Precision Multimeter Digitizer for High Transient Current Calibration
abstract: The calibration of transient current sensors is fundamental for the reliability of high current, short-circuit tests. The test can be performed with prospective or withstand current, but in both cases, the dynamic behavior of the current sensors has to be investigated, due to his influence on the scale factor value. The requirements of the IEe 62475 standard can be achieved with a calibration in transient conditions, performed with an approved reference measuring system. In this work a most performance measuring system is presented, for the improvement of INRIM high transient current measuring capability.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Modeling of BNC-N Adapters
abstract: We present a high-frequency modeling of BNC-N adapters. In the beginning we define a long-line transmission model which was applied to all N and BNC layers of the adapters. Afterwards we calculated the total reflection coefficient of N(m)-BNC(f) adapter // BNC(m)-N(f) adapter // load cascade. The geometry of adapters' layers has been then slightly varied around premeasured values until a good agreement between the simulated and measured reflection coefficient was obtained. This proved the validity of the model and geometry of the adapters which are both indispensable to calculate and apply appropriate corrections that are needed when using BNC-N adapters.

articleTitle: A Self-Calibrated Transfer Standard for Microwave Calorimetry
abstract: We developed a new calibration technique for measuring the correction factor of a calorimeter with a vector network analyzer. Based on a wave-parameter formulation, we developed analytic formulas for the correction-factor (g) and effective-efficiency (η). This allows us to calibrate both the calorimeter and the thermistor mount in a single step. This greatly reduces the number of physical parameters involved in calibration processes while tracking correlated uncertainty.

articleTitle: High Voltage CT Ratio Errors Dependency on Voltage and Power Factor of the Metered Load
abstract: This paper describes the results of performance evaluation of ratio errors of a high voltage current transformer (CT) and a high voltage combined current and voltage transformer (CT/VT) with the aim of discovering the behavior of the CT ratio errors at different operating high voltages, different power factor loads on the transmission line in which the CT (or CT part of the CT/VT) was connected and the effects of the VT burden (in case of the CT/VT).

articleTitle: The Status of the NIM-2 Joule Balance
abstract: The NIM-2 joule balance has been constructed since 2013 and was ready for measurement in vacuum by the end of 2016. In May of 2017, the first result obtained in vacuum with an uncertainty of 2.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> was submitted for publishing. The main uncertainty contributions are from the external field, alignment, mass calibration and others. To decrease these uncertainty contributions and get an uncertainty of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> level, a series of approaches are presented here and will be performed in the near future.

articleTitle: Scaling of Mass and Force Using Electrical Metrology
abstract: The impending redefinition of the International System of Units (SI) allows realization of the kilogram using electrical metrology. It can be shown that electrical metrology can also be used to scale mass using electrostatic forces. An approach to mass metrology at the milligram scale using an Electrostatic Force Balance (EFB) is described. The relative uncertainty in EFB mass measurements is found to be substantially lower than those obtained with the current method based on subdivision of the artifact kilogram.

articleTitle: Method for the Absolute Calibration of Direct-Current Current Transducers
abstract: This paper describes an absolute method for calibrating commercial 1000:1 DC current transducers (DCCTs). By adding two auxiliary windings to produce 10:1 and 100:1 ratios, we use a three-step build-up method to establish the 1000:1 current ratio standard. First, we determine the 10:1 ratios of 11 DCCTs through permutation; second, we set up a two-stage composite DCCT to produce a 100:1 ratio; after switching auxiliary windings in the two-stage setup, we then derive the 1000:1 current ratio. The experimental results will be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Calibration of Electricity Meters with Digital Input
abstract: Over recent decades, proliferation of harmonic producing loads in the electric power system is noticeable, due to, in large part, increase in use of many power electronics devices. The role of power electronics in Smart Grid developments is very important. Smart Grid is characterized by the use of intelligent electronic devices in digital substations, for monitoring, control, protection and metering, based on voltage and current sampled values (SVs) conforming to lEC 61850-9-2 format. The SVs are used for revenue metering by non-conventional energy meters with digital inputs. The paper discusses the performance of these electricity meters under non-sinusoidal waveform conditions.

articleTitle: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Study on a 28Si Single Crystal for the Future Realization of the Kilogram
abstract: In the future realization of the kilogram using the x-ray crystal density method, isotopically enriched silicon crystals grown by the floating zone method are employed. In this paper, we present the electron paramagnetic resonance study on <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si single crystal AVO28. We revealed that the concentrations of various kinds of vacancy defects in the crystal are less than 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. Consequently, the necessary mass deficit correction due to these vacancy defects is estimated to be less than 0.4 μg for 1 kg AVO28 spheres.

articleTitle: Precision Measurement of 1 MΩ Quantum Hall Resistance Array
abstract: We present preliminary results of precision measurements of 1 MΩ quantum Hall resistance array made of the GaAsl AIGaAs heterosubstrate. Precision measurements have been performed with a cryogenic current comparator resistance bridge by comparing the array resistance to a 10 kΩ resistance standard traceable to the quantum Hall effect. Stability of the quantization in the array within the relative standard uncertainty of 18 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> through repeated thermal cycles reflects the invariant quantum nature of the array resistance in a given condition.

articleTitle: Thermal Noise Metrology with Time-Based Synthesis
abstract: We present a new measurement technique for quantifying noise temperature based On temperature and time. A single-pole, double-throw (SPDT) ultra-fast switch combines signals from outputs of two synchronized electromechanical (EM) switches. The input ports of EM switches are terminated by one unknown noise source, one known cold noise source, and two known noise references at ambient temperature. The magnitude of the combined noise signal can be adjusted by the duty cycle of the transistor-transistor logic (TTL) pulse that controls the fast switch. The measurement approaches the balanced mode by regulating the TTL duty cycle in order to minimize the difference between the combined noise signal and the ambient noise reference. In comparison to conventional total-power radiometers, this new instrumentation is more efficient and potentially provides a wider dynamic range.

articleTitle: Quantum voltage noise source chip development at NIM
abstract: Quantum voltage noise source (QVNS) based Johnson noise thermometer (JNT) system employing Josephson junctions (JJs) to generate calculable and quantum accurate pseudo-noise waveform as an artificial noise in measuring the thermodynamic temperature of a resistor. In this paper, we present the design, fabrication, and the primarily characterization of the QVNS chip in NIM.

articleTitle: A Proposal of LISN Electrical Impedance Calibration
abstract: In this paper, a proposal of LISN impedance calibration will be presented, by means of the measurement of the reflection coefficient magnitude and its respective phase, using a VNA. The procedure for determining the respective measurement uncertainties obtained by Monte Carlo method will be described. The results of a LISN calibration will also be presented.

articleTitle: Optical Transition Edge Sensors: Wavelength Dependence of System Detection Efficiency
abstract: Optical transition edge sensors (TESs) which can resolve an energy of a single photon have proven desirable in quantum information and biology. TESs can provide spectra ranging from near-infrared to visible regions, and have the potential to reveal new phenomena in biology. To obtain reliable spectra, wavelength dependence of the system detection efficiency should be calibrated. The dependence is due to a cavity structure of the detector, consisting of an anti-reflection coating and a mirror. We will present a calibration using a supercontinuum laser and acousto-optic tunable filters (AOTF).

articleTitle: Observation of Solder Layers for PJVS Chips Formed with Supersonic-Soldering Method
abstract: The InSn solder layers between Si chips for programmable Josephson voltage standard (PJVS) and sapphire substrates for thermal contact were observed using a scanning acoustic microscope. The solder layers were formed with a supersonic-soldering method in several conditions. Based on the results of the observations, the void ratio in the solder layers was estimated to be approximately 20 % - 40 %, which is much improved in comparison to that obtained with a conventional soldering method of approximately 80 %. We are now trying to measure the influence of these soldering methods on the thermal contact of PJVS chips.

articleTitle: Linearity Testing of High Precision Digital Voltmeters with Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) recently established in TÜBİTAK UME, is used to investigate the linearity of the high precision digital voltmeters (DVM). The new system with fast settling and stable output voltages is an efficient tool to test DVM linearity from 0 to ±10V with an uncertainty better than 0.1 μV/V.

articleTitle: Extension of a Waveform Reconstruction Algorithm for a DVM with an Integrating ADC
abstract: This paper describes the design of an amplitude equalizer for digital voltmeters (DVM) with an integrating ADC (IADC). It is suggested to use the equalizer in combination with all-pass filters that correct nonlinearity of the phase characteristic of the measurement channels. The proposed filters will be able to eliminate the effect of the IADC and signal conditioning circuits at up to 20 % of the sampling frequency.

articleTitle: Reference System for the Practical Peak Voltage Calibration in Radiology and Diagnostic Applications
abstract: Practical Peak Voltage (PPV) has been recently adopted by IEC as a new quantity to qualify the pulsed voltages applied to X-ray high voltage tubes. Two commercial invasive dividers are characterized for every x-ray pulses for voltage up to 150 kV and for exposure time between 200 μs and few seconds. The measurement of impulse low current flowing through X-ray tubes is carried out non-invasively by using a clamp meter based on Hall Effect. Deconvolution technique is used to enhance the accuracy of the reference system.

articleTitle: Study of Keysight 3458A Temperature Coefficient for Different Aperture Times in DCV Sampling Mode
abstract: A study of DCV sampling mode Keysight 3458A digital multimeter (DMM) temperature coefficient is presented. For different DMMs, a set of digital measurements at different temperatures and aperture times has been performed, to establish DMMs gain variation with temperature. Results confirm the existence of two different temperature coefficients, for high-resolution and high-speed stages. While for the first one values in the range of 0.1 μV/V°C are obtained, for high speed stage values can be in the order of 10 μV/V°C, which should be taken into account for its compensation in high accuracy measurement.

articleTitle: The Design and Development of a Tabletop Kibble Balance at NIST
abstract: A global paradigm shift to redefine the International System of Units (SI) from a system based on seven fundamental units to seven fundamental constants is well under way. More specifically, the unit of mass, the kilogram, will be realized via a fixed value of the Planck constant h and a Kibble balance (KB) serves as a method of achieving this. Over the past few decades, national metrology institutes around the world have invested in developing KBs, the majority aimed at realizing the unit of mass at the I-kg level with uncertainties on the order of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. However, upon fixing the Planck constant, mass can be directly realized at any level, deeming the kilogram only a historically unique benchmark. At the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), a tabletop-sized Kibble balance (KIBB-gI) designed to operate at the gram-level range with uncertainties on the order of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> is currently under development.

articleTitle: A Self-Gap-Correction Method for Broadband Measurement of Complex Permittivity
abstract: A novel self-gap-correction method for accurately measuring the broadband permittivity of materials based on the transmission/reflection theory is proposed. A combination strategy of the electromagnetic finite element simulation (FEM) and a hybrid optimization algorithm is employed to rapidly extract the true values of the gap size and permittivity. This method relaxes the fully filled assumption of the test specimens and realizes the self-correction of air-gap effect without requiring its exact size. The high accuracy and practical suitability of the proposed method are validated through experimental tests.

articleTitle: Metrological Challenge for Scanning Microwave Microscopy
abstract: We have demonstrated a near-field scanning microwave microscopy (SMM) based on an atomic force microscopy (AFM) with interferometric circuits for characterization of high permittivity dielectric materials. Fixed impedance matching technique is generally used in commercial SMM product. We propose a passive interferometer circuit is applied to SMM system in prototype or laboratory level system. All system is useful for operators without knowledge of microwave measurements, but they have somewhat limitation of measurement range in order to characterization of high dielectric permittivity materials. Then, we demonstrate high-precision characterization for high permittivity dielectric materials by our SMM system with passive interferometric detection circuit.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Metrology for NEMS
abstract: This paper outlines how demands on electromagnetic metrology have developed over recent years with the continuing reduction in the typical length scale of electronic components and circuits. In addition novel materials, especially 2D self-supporting structures such as graphene, have properties quite unlike conventional systems. At the nanoscale radical changes occur in techniques required and even in the physical quantities measured. This paper focusses on the example of a nearfield scanning microwave microscope and its application to nanoelectromechanical system resonators to illustrate these changes and challenges.

articleTitle: A Switch-Controller for Improved Measurements in the NIST Magnetic Suspension Mass Comparator
abstract: We describe a switch-based control strategy implemented on a proof-of-concept version of the Magnetic Suspension Mass Comparator (MSMC) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology. The MSMC apparatus is used to compare mass artifacts held in air to mass artifacts held in vacuum, without having to remove either artifact from its respective environment; thus, eliminating the need to use empirical sorption models. This comparison is achieved by magnetically suspending the mass artifact held in air. The switch-controller utilizes a combination of a magnetic field and displacement measurement to achieve the desired robustness and stability.

articleTitle: Traceability Chain Establishment at KRISS from DC QHR to Farad Using AC-DC Calculable Resistor Standard and Digitally Assisted Coaxial Bridges
abstract: A national traceability chain from dc quantum Hall resistance (QHR) to capacitance has been established at KRISS using various impedance standards and ac coaxial bridges. Two bridges developed by INRiM, were employed: a quadrature bridge, calibrating 1000 pF capacitors versus 103 kΩ ac resistors and a ratio bridge, linking the ac resistor values to an ac-dc calculable resistor calibrated in terms of the dc QHR. The capacitance value obtained with the new traceability chain showed an agreement (a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>) in a comparison with the scale maintained at National Institute for Standards and Technology (NIST, USA).

articleTitle: Multicomponent Force and Torque Measurement in the New SI
abstract: A multicomponent force and torque sensor with an integrated calibration system is shown. The calibration factors for the sensor are determined using voltage, resistance, position, angle and time references. In this way, the force and torque measurements can be traced directly to fundamental physical constants, with many advantages when compared to traditional methods. A prototype designed for measuring forces and torques in a range of 2 N and 0.1 N·m with a relative combined standard uncertainty (k=2) of \pmb10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> is currently being implemented. Preliminary experimental results used to evaluate some aspects of the system's performance are presented.

articleTitle: Open-Source Package for PJVS Testing and Calibration
abstract: This paper describes a software package for PJVS automated measurements written in Python, an interpreted programming language widely used in scientific applications. The code is modular and expandable with the support of many libraries allowing easy reconfiguration for different calibration and testing purposes.

articleTitle: A Method for Realisation of Inductance and Quality Factor to 1 MHz
abstract: This paper describes a method for realisation of inductance and quality factor to high frequencies by determining the frequency response of gain-and phase-error of an inductance meter using two coils made of a single copper wire. As a starting point a traceable calibration of inductance at 1 kHz is used.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two High Accuracy Room Temperature Methods to Calibrate a 10 kΩ Standard with the Quantized Hall Resistance
abstract: This paper describes a comparison of two methods to calibrate a 10 kΩ standard resistor respect to the Quantized Hall Resistance (QHR). One method is based in a Room Temperature Current Comparator Bridge and the other one is based in a Resistive Transfer Standard (RTS) developed at CEM in its different configurations, one of which is the QHR value. In this way we'll test the suitability of both methods to perform QHR measurements.

articleTitle: Towards an Improved Programmable Quantum Current Generator
abstract: We report on a noise characterization and some on-going improvements of a programmable quantum current generator (PQCG) based on the extension of Ohm's law to quantum standards.

articleTitle: Transport of NIST Graphene Quantized Hall Devices and Comparison with AIST Gallium-Arsenide Quantized Hall Devices
abstract: Two graphene quantized Hall resistance (QHR) devices made at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) were hand carried to the National Institute for Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) and compared to a GaAs QHR device and a \pmb100 Ω standard resistor. Measurement of the \pmb100 Ω resistor with the graphene QHR devices agreed within \pmb5 x \pmb10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> of the \pmb100 Ω resistor GaAs measurements. After the initial measurements, the carrier density of the graphene devices was adjusted at AIST to restore the device properties to operate at low magnetic fields of 4 T to 6 T.

articleTitle: Persistence of Electromagnetic Units in Magnetism
abstract: The centimeter-gram-second system of electromagnetic units (EMU) has been used in magnetism since the late 19th century. The International System of Units (SI), a successor to Giorgi's 1901 meter-kilogram-second system, was adopted by the General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1960. However, EMU remains in common use for the expression of magnetic data. The forthcoming revision of the SI provides an excellent reason for magnetics researchers to abandon the use of EMU.

articleTitle: Development and Fabrication of Improved Josephson Series Arrays with NbSi Barrier for AC Voltage Standards
abstract: Series arrays of overdamped Josephson junctions compose the basis of AC Josephson voltage standards. Presently, an advanced technology is based on Josephson junctions consisting of an Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>barrier. Using junction stacks containing five Josephson junctions, series arrays of 15,000 junctions have been successfully fabricated at PTB for the pulse-driven Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS). The operation of eight arrays simultaneously enable spectrally pure waveforms with output voltages above 1 V to be synthesized.

articleTitle: Design of a Cell-Based Refractometer with Small End-Effects
abstract: In cell-based laser refractometers, interferometer pathlength uncertainty introduced by deformation and stress in the windows through which the beams pass can be the chief factor limiting measurement accuracy. The fractional contribution of pathlength uncertainty to our recent determination of the Boltzmann constant was 9.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, and more than two times larger than the next largest uncertainty component. We briefly describe the error and propose a design in which cell window effects contribute less than 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> fractional error to the measurement of helium refractivity; performance that would be competitive with state-of-the-art primary thermometry and barometry.

articleTitle: 1-Port Vector Network Analyzer Calibration Technique Using Three Lines
abstract: This paper proposes a calibration technique for 1-port vector network analyzers (VNA) using three lines as the measurement standard. In the method, the reflection coefficient of a device under test and the circuit errors, such as the directivity, matching, and tracking, are simultaneously obtained. The advantage of the method is that results without the effects of the circuit errors are obtained, no assumption is required for the characteristics of the standard lines and theory, and the simple SI traceability can be established.

articleTitle: Characterization of Vapor Adsorption on the Surface of Si Spheres by Ellipsometry
abstract: For the determination of the Avogadro constant using the x-ray crystal density method, surface analysis of Si spheres is essential. The difference of the surface layer thickness in vacuum and in air conditions was investigated by ellipsometry. In order to estimate the effect of vapor adsorption on the determination of the thickness of the surface layer of Si spheres, an ellipsometer with vacuum chamber and vapor controlling system is proposed.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Calibration of ADC Using JAWS
abstract: A new method for the calibration of digitizers was tested. This method uses the unique ability of Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) to generate almost any waveform with high precision. A complex waveform has been prepared such that the gain of a digitizer at different frequencies and amplitudes was calibrated simultaneously. The stability of the gain was also evaluated.

articleTitle: CENAM's Primary Standard for High Frequency Power Up to 50 GHz
abstract: This paper describes a 2.4 mm coaxial microcalorimeter and its associated thermoelectric-type transfer standard/sensor, which together will realize a primary standard for microwave and millimeter wave power from 18 GHz to 50 GHz at Centro Nacional de Metrologia (CENAM), Queretaro, Mexico. It summarizes the calorimeter and transfer standard design characteristics and the principle of calorimeter calibration. First results for the calorimeter and transfer standard/sensor performance are given. The developed data acquisition system to automate the effective efficiency measurements is also presented.

articleTitle: On-Wafer CPW Standards for S-Parameter Measurements of Balanced Circuits Up to 40 GHz
abstract: The Multimode Thru-Reflect-Line (TRL) calibration technique is applied to perform mixed-mode scattering parameter measurements of on-wafer differential circuits. The paper describes the design and the realization of coupled coplanar waveguide (CCPW) standards on quartz (Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O2</sub>) substrate in the Ground-Signal-Ground-Signal-Ground (GSGSG) configuration. Simulation and measurement results for a mismatched transmission line demonstrate the validity of the method up to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Towards Wideband Voltage Scaling to Quantum Standards at the Accuracy of the Stability
abstract: A divider architecture and measurement method to scale arbitrary waveforms to `spectrally pure Josephson Voltage Standards' so called JAWS is presented. The architecture and measurement method are investigated by simulations. Challenging sides of the architecture and the method, and the solutions are defined. The constructed prototype divider and some of the preliminary measurements are presented.

articleTitle: Epitaxial Graphene for High-Current QHE Resistance Standards
abstract: We report the growth of large-area monolayer graphene on the centimeter scale using an optimized growth process allowing for reproducibility and morphology improvements. Magneto-transport measurements on graphene quantum Hall effect devices demonstrate the applicability for high-current quantum resistance metrology.

articleTitle: Investigation of Atmospheric-Pressure Dependence of Compact Detachable Zener Module
abstract: The influence of atmospheric pressure on the DC voltage output of a prototype Zener voltage standard system has been investigated. The system is composed of a compact temperature-controlled Zener module, detachable from an expansion unit with additional battery packs. It can be used not only as a secondary standard but also as a voltage reference for more general purposes. In this study, we placed the compact Zener module in a vacuum chamber and measured its output voltage by changing the air pressure. The results indicate a pressure coefficient of \pmb(0.5±1.2)nV/hPa for the nominal 10 V output.

articleTitle: Conceptual Consequences of the SI
abstract: The SI and its forerunners were largely developed in response to the confusion of multiple electromagnetic unit systems at the start of the 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> century. More than 100 years later, the success of the SI is evidenced by its almost universal acceptance. The adoption of the ampere as the fourth base unit has proved to be a beneficial way of simplifying electromagnetic units. However, an unintended consequence of adopting this system has been the development of several misconceptions regarding the physics of electromagnetic quantities. The anticipated educational activities associated with the upcoming SI redefinition offer an ideal opportunity to resolve this concern.

articleTitle: Signal Modeling for Dynamic Testing of Smart Electricity Meter
abstract: By analyzing the typical large power dynamic loads characteristics, a general dynamic testing signal model and its three-phase m-sequence pseudorandom dynamic testing signal are established. Two kinds of smart electricity meters are measured, and the results are given. Concurrently, the measurement uncertainty was evaluated.

articleTitle: Frequency Accuracy Measurements for the Microwave Generator Used in the Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard at NRC
abstract: Standard frequency and time techniques are used to characterize the frequency accuracy of the commercial microwave generator used in the Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard at National Research Council Canada. Tests are also performed to verify the frequency resolution of the generator.

articleTitle: One-Gate Ratchet Single-Electron Pump: Device Failure Mechanisms
abstract: Electrical current standards based on the charge of the electron will become more important after the SI redefinition. Many of the best recent charge pump results have come in the one-gate ratchet pumping mode, but this mode is sometimes difficult to achieve. In this work, we discuss the likely reasons for this difficulty, and ways to overcome the difficulty.

articleTitle: Quantum Efficiency Measurement of a Photovoltaic Detector by Comparison with a Pyroelectric Detector on Individual Nano-Second Laser Pulses
abstract: We demonstrate that the individual single pulse of a nano-second laser can be used to measure the quantum efficiency of photovoltaic detectors. With this new scheme, the relative quantum efficiency of a photodiode can be determined from the spectral reflectance of the surface of a pyroelectric detector. We also developed the adequate data acquisition procedure, which can eliminate systematic errors caused by the nonlinear pulse response. The method is experimentally demonstrated for Si and Ge photodiodes in a wide wavelength range from 420 nm to 1600 nm and verified by comparison with the method using a CW source.

articleTitle: Improved Sine-Fitting Algorithms for Sampling Measurements of Complex Ratio of AC Voltages
abstract: The article presents a modified sine-fitting algorithms which can be used for high-accuracy sampling measurements of complex voltage ratio of sinusoidal signals. The proposed algorithms provide a significant reduction in the measurement uncertainty of phase shift when synchronizing the sampler and signal source is impossible.

articleTitle: Research on Measurement Uncertainty of Absorption Cross Section in a Reverberation Chamber
abstract: The absorption cross section (ACS) of absorbers are measured in a reverberation chamber and the relative uncertainty of measurements is calculated. The ACS is calculated by a time-domain method at frequencies in the range 1-3GHz. The average relative uncertainty of the ACS over the frequency range is 0.02 by the measurements in eight different configurations of absorbers and antennas, which shows good experimental stability.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity of the NIST Calculable Capacitor
abstract: We reexamine nonlinearity of the NIST calculable capacitor which is used for realizing the capacitance unit. The “end-effect” is apparent close to the 0.7 pF position. Improved accuracy can be achieved by operating the instrument from 0.2 pF to 0.6 pF.

articleTitle: Comparison and Voltage Dependence Measurement in Phase Angle Errors of Two Voltage Dividers
abstract: This paper describes the design and self-calibration in phase angle errors of the RVD with serial-parallel connection and IVD with cascade structure. The self-calibration results have been verified with a comparison experiment at frequencies up to 100 kHz. The voltage dependence in phase angle errors of the two voltage dividers has also been calibrated from 64 V to 300 V and the measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Harmonic Power Standard of VTT MIKES
abstract: This paper describes the new single-phase harmonic power standard of VTT MIKES. The standard is based on a custom digitizer, which is developed for AC metrology in the laboratory, and for field measurement campaigns. Test signal generation uses a dual channel arbitrary function generator, a voltage amplifier, and a transconductance amplifier. Reference voltage and current measurements are respectively based on a capacitive-resistive voltage divider and two different types of resistive shunt designs.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Power Quality Changing Parameters Using DFT Coefficients
abstract: In paper, algorithms for fast measurement and estimation of the changing frequency components parameters and other power parameters for evaluation of the power quality disturbances, are presented. Parameters are calculated from the largest local DFT coefficients of particular frequency components. The improvement for reducing the influences of the harmonic components is the estimation below or equal to one signal period.

articleTitle: Cryocooler Operation of a DC Voltage Standard Based on High Temperature Superconductor Josephson Junctions
abstract: A commercially available Josephson voltage standard based on high temperature superconductor Josephson junctions with a liquid nitrogen free cooling is presented. The results of the calibrations of an electronic DC reference Fluke 732B and a Keithley nanovoltmeter 2182 with uncertainties equal to a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> demonstrate the suitability of the application of a N4-21 in the highest-level metrology. The implementation of a link between Josephson junctions and Zener diodes largely eliminates the uncertainty contributions associated with Zeners non-linear drift, environmental effects and the impact due to shipping.

articleTitle: External-Reference Stabilized Current Source with Sub-PPM Stability
abstract: The noise and stability of a commercial current source is limited by the quality of components used for construction, such as the voltage reference chips, resistors, and power supplies. A state-of-the-art commercial current source typically exhibits a stability no better than parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>. In this paper, we present a way to implement a current source with “external” electrical references. This approach allows the current source stability to be decoupled from the noise characteristics of the main power supply circuit. A few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> stability is demonstrated here.

articleTitle: Single-Photon Avalanche Detector Calibration at PTB
abstract: In this paper we present the traceable calibration of the detection efficiency of Si and InGaAs/InP single-photon avalanche detectors (SPADs). We describe the calibration facilities and the reference standard detectors used, as well as the traceability chain of the measurements to the primary standard for optical power (Cryogenic Radiometer) of PTB. As an example, the detection efficiency of a Si and InGaAs/InP SPAD detector measured at wavelengths of 850 nm and 1550 nm, respectively, for different photon flux rates is presented. The standard uncertainty of the measurements is ≤ 1 %.

articleTitle: Limitations to the Short-Term Stability of 100 MΩ and 1 GΩ Standard Resistors
abstract: We find that a sample of commercially-available 100 MΩ and 1 GΩ standard resistors exhibit 1/f behavior in their measured value on time-scales longer than ≈ 1 hour. In practice, this means the resistance cannot be specified with an uncertainty smaller than about 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>.

articleTitle: Progress on Simple Resistance Standard with Calculable Time Constant
abstract: This paper describes the progress on the development of the simple calculable bifilar resistors with nominal resistance below 100 Ω. The resistor have very simple and cheap construction that can be easily replicated. It is based on the ordinary circular cross-section resistance wire with enamel layer. Detailed characterization of the wire was made and thus the expanded uncertainty (k = 2) of the resistance is as low as 34 μΩ/Ω at 1 MHz. The expanded uncertainty of the time constant is below 0.11 ns (680 μrad/MHz).
